FULL AND UNCONDITIONAL PARDON
Pursuant to the authority vested in me under Article IV, Section 7, of the Colorado
Constitution and the laws of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of
Colorado, do hereby issue this Executive Order granting a pardon to Troy A. Gill.
1. Background and Need
Troy A. Gill was convicted in 1997 of theft in Weld County, Colorado. He was sentenced to
two years probation. The District Attorney and Judge have no objection to the granting of
this pardon. The Executive Clemency Advisory Board has reviewed and considered this
application for clemency and, based upon his rehabilitation and good character, recommends
this pardon.
2. Directive
I hereby order the following:
Troy A. Gill is pardoned of the 1997 crime of theft, committed in Weld County,
Colorado.
All of his rights of citizenship, including but not limited to, voting, jury duty,
holding public office and firearms privileges, are restored in full without
condition. All of his civil disabilities and public sufferings associated with this
conviction are removed and this pardon shall assist him with all public
licensing, certification and employment requirements.

EFFICIENT MANAGEMENT OF STATE EMPLOYEE TRAVEL EXPENSES
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I,
Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order amending
Executive Order D 005 03, addressing state employee travel expenses.
1. Background and Purpose
Executive Order D 005 03 ("Concerning State Employee Travel") established policies and
procedures intended to reduce expenses for state employee travel. One element of that Order
required the Department of Personnel and Administration to develop rules requiring
submission of receipts for reimbursement of per diem allowances unless the travel purchases
were approved in writing. This policy has caused large administrative cost increases but has
produced no demonstrable savings.
2. Directive
I hereby amend Executive Order D 005 03 to eliminate the third paragraph of section 2(A),
which required that state employees submit receipts for reimbursement of state travel per
diem allowances.
3. Duration
This Executive Order shall remain in force until modified or rescinded by further executive
order of the Governor.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Directing the Colorado Commission on Low-Income Energy Assistance to Coordinate the
State's Low-Income Energy Services
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill
Ritter, Jr., Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing the
Colorado Commission on Low-Income Energy Assistance to coordinate the state's low-income
energy services.
1. Background and Purpose
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is the recipient of funds under the Low-
Income Home Energy Assistance Act of 1981 (P.L. 97-35), hereafter referred to as the Low-
Income Energy Assistance Program ("LEAP"). The Colorado Department of Human Services is
the administrator of LEAP and receives state and federal funds to provide utility bill assistance
and crisis intervention services. The Colorado Department of Human Services allocates up to
15% of the Federal LEAP Block Grant to the Governor's Energy Office, which in turn, is
combined with other federal and state funds to provide weatherization services. Pursuant to
C.R.S § 40-8.7-103(4), Energy Outreach Colorado, also receives state funding to assist low-
income energy consumers. The Colorado Commission on Low-Income Energy Assistance was
established pursuant to C.R.S. § 40-8.5-103.5, and its membership includes representatives from
LEAP, the Governor's Energy Office, and Energy Outreach Colorado. Based upon its
membership and expertise, the Colorado Commission on Low-Income Energy Assistance is the
appropriate body to coordinate the state's low-income energy services.
2.
Mission, Scope, and Directives
I hereby designate the Colorado Commission on Low-Income Energy Assistance
("Commission") as the entity responsible for coordinating the state's low-income energy
assistance services.
The administrators of the state's LEAP and weatherization services shall report to the
Commission on a quarterly basis. At a minimum such reporting shall include: proposed policy
or regulatory changes; information regarding funding and expenditures; and information
---PAGE---
regarding service goals and measurable results. The Commission shall request comparable
information from Energy Outreach Colorado concerning state-funded services.
The Governor's Energy Office, the Colorado Department of Human Services, and Energy
Outreach Colorado shall provide to the Commission other data or information relevant to
assessing the current status of Colorado's low-income energy consumers. The Commission is to
engage other state departments, agencies, and any utilities that receive LEAP funds on behalf of
their low-income customers in the sharing of pertinent data and information.
The Commission is to make recommendations to the Governor concerning opportunities to
improve the state's overall response to low-income energy consumers, including, but not limited
to:
• how best to target the state's low-income energy services resources toward the
identified needs;
• how best to coordinate public and private energy assistance activities with the
objective of minimizing the financial burden of energy costs for Colorado's most
needy;
• how best to streamline administrative processes, such as outreach, intake, and
eligibility determination;
• a process for annually reviewing anticipated needs, determining anticipated available
resources, recommending an allocation of the available resources via the various
service delivery channels; and
• proposals for changes in state statutes, rules, or polices pertinent to low-income
energy consumers in Colorado.
3. Duration
This Executive Order shall remain in effect until modified or rescinded by the Governor.
GIVEN under my hand and
the Executive Seal of the
State of Colorado, this 24"h
day of October, 2007.

driven by gusty winds and fed by dry fuels. Two additional wildfires started to the
northeast of the Bear Fire and quickly burned together creating the Purgatoire Fire.

Division of Emergency Management, Department of Corrections and local emergency
teams, have responded to the wildfire by deploying a variety of resources, including over
116 firefighters, 7 engines, 3 bulldozers and 3 helicopters.

disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, defines a disaster as "the
occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not
limited to ... fire." C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). The Bear Fire's and Purgatoire Fire's
proximity to ranch headquarters, the towns of Trinidad, Trinchera, and Raton, and state
highway 160 pose an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore, constitute a
disaster for the purposes of the Act. In response to this disaster, on May 28, 2011, I
declared a disaster emergency.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and consistent
with the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC), C.R.S. § 24-60-2902, John W.
Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issues this Executive Order authorizing
the deployment of certain Colorado National Guard resources to assist in flood fighting in, and at
the request of, the State of Nebraska.
I.
Background and Purpose
Nebraska has experienced and is expecting significant rising waters in the Platte River Basin
which will likely cause significant flooding, property damage and potential danger to citizens.
The Governor of Nebraska has declared a state disaster and has validated to the State of
Colorado that Nebraska is threatened by that emergency disaster. In order to mitigate the threat
of flooding, Nebraska is undertaking sandbagging operations and requires the support of a UH-
60 helicopter, pilots, and crew chief in the North Platte, Nebraska area.
On June 21", 2011, the State of Nebraska filed with the State of Colorado an EMAC "Form REQ
A, 2011" requesting said resources by June 22"d,
, 2011, to be released July 1S!
2011.
A previous EMAC request from the State of Nebraska for the same purpose and identical
Colorado National Guard assets was granted pursuant to Executive Order D 2011-019, executed
on June 13t*, 2011. However, the State of Nebraska has determined that additional Colorado
National Guard resources are necessary given the risk the situation poses to lives of Nebraska
citizens.
I find that the conditions under which such resources can be made available and used to meet the
emergency needs of the State of Nebraska under the EMAC have been satisfied as a result of the
occurrence and imminent threat of emergency disaster described above.
Il.

A.
The State of Nebraska has communicated that it is experiencing an emergency
disaster occurring within that state which provides a basis for activation of the

Adjutant General to respond to the State of Nebraska's request for National Guard
support of missions required in response to their emergency disaster, as requested by

Pursuant to the EMAC, all relevant costs to the State of Colorado shall be reimbursed
by the State of Nebraska.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Suspending Prescribed or Controlled Fire Pending Review of Protocols
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Colorado Constitution, article IV, section 13 and C.R.S. § 23-31-308,
Joseph A. Garcia, Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issues this Executive
Order suspending prescribed or controlled fire by State agencies pending review of agency
protocols for prescribed or controlled fire.
1.
Background and Purpose
Many areas of Colorado have been experiencing above average temperatures and dry
conditions. As a result, the National Weather Service has issued a number of Red Flag warnings
for the Front Range and other portions of the state. Already this year, Colorado has
experienced several wildfires.
On March 25, 2012, the Lower North Fork Fire may have been started by a prescribed or
controlled fire. As of this issuance of this order, the Lower North Fork Fire had burned
approximately several thousand acres, resulted in the deaths of two people, and destroyed
several homes.
To help respond to the Lower North Fork Fire, on March 27, Lt. Governor Joseph Garcia issued
Executive Oder D 2012-005 that activated the National Guard and activated the State
Emergency Operations Plan.
Prescribed or controlled fire is a tool used to reduce the overabundance of vegetation and
dense stands of trees—in other words, the fuels-that can lead to intense, catastrophic
wildfires. However, it must only be used under the right conditions and under responsible
management.
As a result, given that a prescribed or controlled fire may have been the cause of the Lower
North Fork Fire, the State should suspend further use of this land and fire management tool to
make sure that we have the procedures and protocols in place so that these conditions and
management requirements are understood and strictly followed.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2012-006
March 28, 2012
Page 2 of 2
HI.
Declaration and Directives
A.
I hearby order all State agencies to suspend prescribed or controlled fire on State
or private lands pending review of agency protocols for prescribed or controlled
fire. This suspension applies to all State lands as well as State agencies that
apply prescribed or controlled fire on non-State lands under contracts or
agreements with other entities.
For purposes of this order, "prescribed or controlled fire" is defined as the
controlled application of fire in accordance with a written plan for wildland fuels
under specified environmental conditions while following appropriate
precautionary measures that ensure that the fire is confined to a predetermined
area to accomplish planned fire or land-management objectives.
C.
For purposes of this order, "prescribed or controlled fire" does not apply to
agricultural burning, however, extreme care and caution in agricultural burning is
strongly encouraged. For purposes of this order, "agricultural burning" is
defined as open burning of cover vegetation for the purposes of preparing the
soil for crop production, weed control, maintenance of water conveyance
structures related to agricultural operations, and other agricultural cultivation
purposes.
III.
Duration
This Executive Order shall expire upon review of State agencies' prescribed or controlled fire
protocols or upon rescission by subsequent Executive Order.
Lieutenant Governor
I am executing this Executive Order pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, article IV, section
13(5) as Governor John W. Hickenlooper is currently traveling outside of the State of Colorado.

Cherokee Meadows community and the Boxer Ranch Subdivision. The fire grew rapidly being
fueled by extremely dry vegetation, low relative humidity, high temperatures, and windy

fire department resources have been fully engaged in both evacuating residents from harm's
way and in fighting the wildfire. Predicted hot weather and strong gusty winds coupled with
abundant dry fuels pose a real threat of the fire spreading toward additional state and private
values at risk and indicate an aggressive response is essential. A county Type 3 Incident
Management Team was immediately ordered for the fire along with use of a Single Engine Air
Tanker, a Type 3 Helicopter, eight engines, and a wildfire hand crew.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, defines a disaster as "the occurrence
or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire." C.R.S. §
24-32-2103(1.5). The Stuart Hole Fire's proximity to sub-developments and the town of
Livermore poses an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster
for the purposes of the Act. In response to this disaster, on June 4, 2012, I declared a disaster
emergency.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in

Joseph A. Garcia, Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive
Order declaring of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in Mesa County, Colorado
and making resources available to fight the fire.
1.
Background and Purpose
On Tuesday July 10, 2012, a wildfire ('Bull Basin Fire") started in Mesa County. The fire grew
rapidly being fueled by extremely dry vegetation, low relative humidity, high temperatures, and
windy conditions. The cause of the fire is unknown and is under investigation. As of July 12,
the fire has spread to approximately 20 acres on private land. Mesa County and local fire
department resources have been fully engaged in fighting the wildfire. Predicted hot weather
and strong gusty winds coupled with abundant dry fuels posed a threat of the fire spreading
toward additional state and private lands and indicated an aggressive response.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, defines a disaster as "the occurrence
or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire." C.R.S. §
24-32-2103(1.5). The proximity of the fire in Mesa County to sub-developments and the
extreme growth potential of the fire posed an imminent danger to life and property and,
therefore, constituted a disaster for the purposes of the Act. A disaster was declared on July
10, 2012.

contained within this Executive Order.

appropriate staff and equipment as necessary.

Maintenance Trust Fund into the Disaster Emergency Fund. The Director of the

On June 19, 2013, at approximately 1355 hours, the Lime Gulch Fire was reported to State
authorities near Foxton Road and the South Platte River Road on the Pike National Forest in
Jefferson County. This wind-driven fire was quickly growing in size and intensity, prompting the
mandatory evacuation of area homes. All available firefighting resources were committed to
firefighting and structural protection.
On June 20, 2013, at approximately 0500 hours the Jefferson County Sheriff determined that
the fire had extended from the Pike National Forest and would exceed the ability of the county
and other local resources to contain and extinguish it and requested the response of the
Division of Fire Prevention and Control. The Jefferson County Sheriff requested transfer of the
fire to the State of Colorado under the Emergency Fire Fund (EFF) provisions.
At approximately 1200 hours, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control completed its
assessment and determined that the Lime Gulch Fire met the criteria for EFF designation.
However, EFF funds were exhausted in previous fires. Therefore, a disaster emergency was

John W. Hickenlooper

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104 and relevant portions of the
Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W. Hickenlooper,
Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending the Declaration
of Disaster Emergency and incorporating by reference all sections therein unless specifically
altered below due to the historic flooding of September 2013.
I.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as
"the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to
…..flood." C.R.S. §24-33.5-703(3).
As a result of the historic flooding last September, nine people were killed, 218 people were
injured and over 18,000 people were forced to leave their homes. Additionally, one individual
was killed assisting in the recovery effort. The flooding was widespread and impacted twenty-
four counties. Damage to property has been extensive: 1852 homes have been destroyed and
as of January 29, 2014, 28,364 households have registered with the Federal Emergency
Management Agency ("FEMA"). Over 200 households remain displaced, and FEMA continues
to deploy its direct housing mission to those most severely impacted. Forty-four households
remain in FEMA's manufactured housing. The system to waive state regulatory statutes, or the
orders, rules and regulations of any state agency provided in Executive Order D 2013-027(II)(1)
is still required.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2014-002
February 5, 2014
Page 2 of 2
The State of Colorado, in strong collaboration with local municipalities, the National Guard, the
federal government, and non-governmental organizations, continue to make considerable
progress in rebuilding Colorado's infrastructure. Although all state highways are now open,
flooding of this magnitude caused damage to infrastructure on multiple levels. Over 200

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in

Department of Corrections with a search.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as the "imminent threat
of widespread or severe damage, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any ... cause
of human origin, including but not limited to ... civil disturbance ... condition of riot,
insurrection, or invasion existing in the state or in any county, city, town or district in the state."
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3).
On March 4, 2014, at approximately 2130 hours, four prisoners escaped from the Otero County
Jail. One of the escapees is a Colorado Department of Corrections parolee who was in the
custody of the Otero County Sheriff's Department. The Otero County Sheriff and the Colorado
Department of Corrections deployed ground search assets. At approximately 2300 hours, the
Otero County Sheriff's Office requested the assistance of the Colorado National Guard,
specifically a helicopter with a searchlight and Forward Looking Infrared Radar (FLIR) capability
for search operations. This capability was unavailable to the Otero County Sheriff except
through the Colorado National Guard. Further, because the Department of Corrections has
responsibility for one of the escapees, deployment of state assets to assist was appropriate. At

approximately 2300 hours on March 4, 2014, I verbally authorized the activation of the National
Guard pursuant to C.R.S. 99 28-3-104 and 16-2.5-144. This Executive Order memorializes my
verbal order. Due to weather conditions, the deployment of the helicopter did not occur until
approximately 0800 hours on March 5, 2014. As of 1700 hours on March 5, 2014, three of the
four inmates have been captured and the Otero County Sheriff's Department has assumed
command of the search for the fourth.

emergency under § 24-33.5-701, 705. My verbal orders activating the National Guard
and authorizing the utilization of National Guard assets to assist in the search and to
enforce the laws of the State of Colorado pursuant to C.R.S. §§ 28-3-104 and 16-2.5-144
are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect
of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order.
B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), the demand on the funds regularly appropriated to
the state and local agencies in coping with this disaster are unreasonably great.
Therefore, it is ordered that $50,000 from the Disaster Emergency Fund is encumbered
to pay for the use of the National Guard helicopter. These funds are available in the
Disaster Emergency Fund from unexpended and reimbursed amounts from previous
disasters in 2011 and 2012.

for the described purposes for eighteen months from the date of this Executive Order.

forces, I employ and call to active duty certain elements of the Colorado National

STATE OF COLORADO
OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR
D 2014-011
EXECUTIVE ORDER
Ordering Funds Transferred to the Resource Mobilization
Fund Based on the Imminent Threat of the Impending Wildfire Season
1876
John W. Hickenlooper
Governor
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104 and the Colorado Disaster
Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of
Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring an imminent threat to the lives and
property of the people of the State of Colorado due to the impending wildfire season and
ordering transfer of funds into the State's Resource Mobilization Fund to address fires as
rapidly as they arise.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented
by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire."
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3).
A. Upcoming Fire Season
Wildfires have long posed a risk to the health and safety of the people of Colorado.
However, in recent years, the frequency of these fires has increased tremendously. During the
1960s, Colorado saw an average of 457 wildfires that burned 8,170 acres annually, but by the
1990s, these numbers more than doubled to an average of over 1,300 fires burning 22,000
acres annually. By the end of the 2000s, these numbers had again doubled making even a
normal fire season very dangerous and costly for our community. Experts also predict that the
annual number of fires will continue to increase as drought, beetle kill, and more severe
weather conditions increase the likelihood and complexity of wildfires.
In 2012 alone Colorado saw 6,459 fires that burned over 250,000 acres, killing six
individuals and resulting in $538 million in direct property losses. During 2012 and 2013, the
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2014-011
June 6, 2014
Page 2 of 3
people of Colorado experienced the most destructive fires in the State's recorded history.
Experts warn that such destructive fire seasons are likely to become the "new normal" for
Colorado.
The Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control estimates that, in an average year,
large wildfires in Colorado will burn more than 113,000 acres of land and result in more than
$41 million in fire suppression expenses. Beyond the direct costs of fighting these fires and the
loss of property, the indirect costs to the State are immeasurable but staggering. Indirect costs
communities face include loss of tax and business revenue, stalled tourism, and costs
associated with resulting health problems and loss of life. One study has indicated that the
indirect cost of large wildfires to western states can be up to 30 times greater than the direct
suppression costs.
There is general consensus among all wildfire experts that the single most effective
strategy in containing wildfires is an immediate and rapid response, as this greatly increases the
chances that responders will contain fires while they are small. Thus, the Colorado Division of
Fire Prevention and Control has identified a primary goal of "keeping fires small." Collaboration
between jurisdictions often provides the most effective, if not only way, to respond adequately
to wildfires as soon as they are discovered.
To assist the State in accomplishing the goal of keeping fires small, the General
Assembly in 2013 created a "Resource Mobilization Fund" (RMF). This fund in part provides a
mechanism for governmental agencies to be reimbursed for costs accrued when they respond
outside of their boundaries to aid neighboring jurisdictions. Mutual assistance from nearby
districts is an important element of any immediate response and this fund helps ensure that
agencies responding outside of their jurisdictions will be reimbursed for eligible expenses. A
rapid and aggressive response by all necessary safety personnel is the best way to keep fires
small, save the taxpayer money, and ultimately reduce the risk of loss of life and property.
The threat and danger fires pose even in a "normal" fire season is staggering, and it is
likely the frequency and scope of wildfires will continue to increase due to changing weather
patterns, more severe storms, drought, beetle kill, and increased development. Therefore, I
find that the upcoming wildfire season poses an imminent threat to the life and property of the
people of the State of Colorado. Accordingly, I direct the State Treasurer to transfer $2,000,000
from the Disaster Emergency Fund to the Resource Mobilization Fund.
B. Pipeline Complex Fire
By making this transfer, the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety also
will have the ability to provide reimbursement to State agencies and jurisdictions for prior
incidents. § 24-33.5-705.4(6)(b). As explained below, local responders to the Pipeline Complex
Fire from last year will be able to be reimbursed.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2014-011
June 6, 2014
Page 3 of 3
On July 9, 2013 lightning ignited the Crazy Fire and the Pipeline Fire in the area of the
Fishers Peak Mesa, approximately five to ten miles southeast of Trinidad in Las Animas County.
By July 10, 2013, the Crazy Fire was approximately 40 acres with 90% containment, and the
Pipeline Fire was approximately 75 acres with 0% containment. These two fires were named
the Pipeline Complex Fire. Local firefighting agencies were the first responders and used local
resources to contain the fire. On July 10, 2013, in order to prevent the fire from becoming a
disaster emergency and to reduce ultimate costs, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control
requested and gained approval of Resource Mobilization as provided in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4.
Local firefighting agencies have sought, but not yet received, reimbursement from the State for
their initial expenditures related to the Pipeline Complex Fire.
By this Executive Order, in addition to making funds available for resource mobilization
for this upcoming fire season, the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety is
hereby authorized to reimburse local firefighting agencies for expenditures related to the
Pipeline Complex Fire from the Resource Mobilization Fund.
1l.
Declaration and Directives
A. Given Colorado's recent history of devastating fires and the nature of the upcoming
wildfire season, I determine that a disaster emergency is imminent pursuant to C.R.S.
§ 24-33.5-706(4.5)(a). I direct the State Treasurer to transfer $2,000,000 from the
Disaster Emergency Fund established by C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a) to the Resource
Mobilization Fund established by C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(6).
B. The Emergency Management Director is hereby authorized to use monies from the
Resource Mobilization Fund to provide reimbursement to State agencies for the costs
they expended during the Pipeline Complex Fire in accordance with
C.R.S. § 24-35-705.4(6)(b).
CUTIVI
GIVEN under my hand and the
Executive Seal of the State of
- the Cou
Governor

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104 and relevant portions of the
Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W. Hickenlooper,
Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order rescinding and replacing
funding provisions of prior executive orders concerning the historic flooding of September
2013.
1.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as
"the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause... including but not limited to... flood." C.R.S.
§ 24-33.5-703(3).
Due to the historic flooding in September 2013, I issued nine executive orders to
address the enormous challenges faced by the people of Colorado. As background, I issued
Executive Order D 2013-026 on September 13, 2013, in the immediate aftermath of the
flooding. This executive order declared a disaster emergency and ordered an initial transfer of
$6,000,000 from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund into the Disaster Emergency Fund. In
assessing the magnitude of the flooding, our office quickly realized that this initial transfer was
not sufficient to address the critical need. Therefore, on September 19, 2013, I issued Executive
Order D 2013-027, which transferred an additional $20,000,000 (for a total of $26,000,000) into
the Disaster Emergency Fund from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2014-012
June 20, 2014
Page 2 of 3
As flood recovery efforts continued throughout September, I again found that the funds
in the Disaster Emergency Fund were insufficient to pay for the flood response and recovery.
On September 26, 2013, I issued Executive Order D 2013-028, which supplemented the
previous transfers into the Disaster Emergency Fund with an extra $65,500,000. As explained
therein, I ordered the transfer of the following amounts into the Disaster Emergency Fund: 1)
$15,500,000 from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund; and 2) $50,000,000 from the
General Fund appropriation in Fiscal Year 2013-14 to the Department of Health Care Policy and
Financing Medical Services Premiums line item. Subsequently, I reduced the amount
transferred from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund from $15,500,000 to $12,950,000 (see
Executive Order D 2013-031). The reason for this change was that sufficient funds remained in
the Disaster Emergency Fund to encumber $65,500,000 for flood-related expenses without
such a large transfer from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund.
In sum, I have ordered the transfer of $91,500,000 into the Disaster Emergency Fund for
response and recovery efforts. The General Assembly reconvened in January 2014.
Recognizing the extraordinary need for additional funding beyond what had already been
ordered, it passed House Bill 14-1245 (titled "Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of
Public Safety"). This bill appropriated $70,000,000 from the General Fund into the Disaster
Emergency Fund. The intent of the bill was to place enough funds in the Disaster Emergency
Fund so that the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing could recover the
$50,000,000 that was used in the immediate aftermath of the floods. Further, the bill
appropriated $20,000,000 beyond what had been transferred to the Disaster Emergency Fund
through prior executive orders, bringing the total amount for flood response and recovery to
$111,500,000. I signed HB 14-1245 into law on February 27, 2014.
This Executive Order clarifies the financing of the Disaster Emergency Fund and sets
aside additional funds for response and recovery efforts in the wake of the September 2013
floods.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2014-012
June 20, 2014
Page 3 of 3
Declaration and Directive
Paragraph II(C) of Executive Orders D 2013-026 and D 2013-027 and Paragraph II (B) of
Executive Orders D 2013-028, D 2013-031, D 2013-033, and D 2014-001 are hereby rescinded
and replaced to read as follows:
Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4) the funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are found
to be insufficient to pay for the flood response and recovery. Therefore, it is ordered that
$38,950,000 be transferred into the Disaster Emergency Fund from the Controlled
Maintenance Trust Fund established in C.R.S. § 24-75-302.5. It is further ordered that
$111,500,000 from the Disaster Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for the flood
response and recovery. The Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby
authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies
and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms
to effect the allocation of the funds. The Director of the Office of Emergency
Management is also authorized to allocate up to $20,000,000 to be used as short-term,
no interest advances in order to provide any political subdivision of the state with short-
term capital needed for flood response and recovery. These funds shall remain available
for this purpose for thirty-six months from December 9, 2013, and any unexpended funds
shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund.

in Fremont County near mile marker 11 on County Road 67. The fire was named the Eight Mile
Fire and initial fire management objectives were to confine and contain the fire. By the evening
of June 27, 2014, the fire had grown to over 400 acres and the Fremont County Sheriff issued
pre-evacuation notices to the sixteen residences in the Red Rocks Subdivision nearby.
An Interagency Type II Incident Management Team was assigned to manage the Eight
Mile Fire. On the morning of June 28, 2014, they made a request through the Pueblo
Interagency Fire Center for a Colorado National Guard helicopter to be on standby for the
emergency removal of assigned personnel for medical purposes. State personnel and the fire
managers agreed to make the helicopter available at Buckley Air Force Base. Later in the day
on June 28, 2014, the State of Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency
Management received a valid resource order from the Pueblo Interagency Dispatch Center with
appropriate financial codes committing the Bureau of Land Management to reimburse the
State of Colorado for the cost of the helicopter mission. I then verbally approved the Division's
request for a National Guard Helicopter at approximately 1100 hours on June 28, 2014.

Background and Purpose
On Wednesday, July 23, 2014, lightning ignited a fire on Bureau of Land Management
("BLM") lands in Eagle County. The fire was named the Bullet Fire, and the initial fire
management objectives were to confine and contain the fire. The fire was burning in rugged
terrain and a Type 1 initial attack helicopter was needed to contain the fire. Unfortunately, due
to other fire activity in the region and throughout the western United States, no Type 1
helicopters were available. As a result, BLM personnel made a request to the High Altitude
Aviation Training Site ("HAATS") for a National Guard helicopter with bucket capability and
associated personnel. Pursuant to his authority under Department of Defense Directive
3025.18, the Commander of HAATS authorized a Colorado National Guard helicopter and
associated personnel to respond. This directive requires that "civil authorities shall be informed
that oral requests for assistance in an emergency must be followed by a written request that
includes an offer to reimburse the Department of Defense at the earliest available
opportunity."
Later in the day of July 23, 2014, the BLM made an official request to the State of
Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management ("DHSEM") through
Grand Junction Interagency Dispatch Center for use of the Colorado National Guard helicopter
for fire suppression. DHSEM then made a request for use of a National Guard Helicopter to the
Governor's Office. Lieutenant Governor Joseph Garcia, acting on behalf of the Governor, then
verbally approved the request at approximately 1557 hours on July 23, 2014. DHSEM
---PAGE---

subsequently received a valid resource order from the Grand Junction Interagency Dispatch
Center committing the BLM to reimburse the State of Colorado for the cost of the helicopter
mission. The use of the Colorado National Guard helicopter was successful and the fire was
contained on July 23, 2014.

helicopter. Ultimately, the BLM will reimburse the Resource Mobilization
Fund for the actual costs expended for the National Guard helicopter and

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104, and to Article IV Section 2 of the

the National Guard and authorizing the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety to
encumber funds from the Resource Mobilization Fund for the purpose of assisting with the
response to the Tonahutu Fire in Rocky Mountain National Park, Grand County, Colorado.
Background and Purpose
On Tuesday, August 12, 2014, a small fire was reported in Rocky Mountain National Park
near the Tonahutu Trail. This fire, named the Tonahutu Fire, is in rugged terrain accessible only
by air or by foot. By nightfall the fire grew to approximately one acre in size. The probable
cause of the fire is lightning.
At approximately 1000 hours on August 13, 2014, the Rocky Mountain Area
Coordination Center requested that the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency
Management ('DHSEM") place a Colorado National Guard helicopter on standby for the
emergency removal of people for medical purposes. DHSEM then made a request to the
Governor's Office for approval for use of a National Guard Helicopter. I verbally approved the
request at approximately 1030 hours on August 13, 2014. DHSEM subsequently received a
valid resource order from the Rocky Mountain Area Coordination Center committing the
National Park Service to reimburse the State of Colorado for the cost of the helicopter mission.
Il.

National Guard for up to 30 days, is hereby memorialized and shall have
the full force and effect of law as if it were contained in this Executive
Order.

Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W. Hickenlooper,
Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending the availability
of funds to pay for costs associated with the disaster emergency due to the June 2013 West
Fork Fire Complex in Hinsdale, Mineral, and Rio Grande Counties, Colorado.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as
"the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to
fire." C.R.S. §24-33.5-703(3).
In June 2013, a series of fires combined to form the West Fork Fire Complex. These fires
grew to over 100,000 acres and led to a mandatory evacuation east of the Continental Divide
including the Town of South Fork. In response to these fires, all available firefighting resources
were deployed. Our office declared a disaster emergency due to West Fork Fire Complex in
Executive Order D 2013-017, which was subsequently amended in Executive Orders D 2013-020
and D 2013-022. We transferred a total of $12,500,000 to the Disaster Emergency Fund from
the 2012-2013 and 2013-2014 appropriations for the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund for
fire suppression, response, and recovery efforts. Of those funds, $195,000 was designated
specifically for funding of recovery efforts. The funds transferred into the Disaster Emergency
Fund for West Fork Fire Complex have been made available until December 26, 2014.
---PAGE---

October 20, 2014
Page 2 of 3

Division of Fire Prevention and Control, and the Federal Emergency Management Agency to
process expenditures and payments for all fire suppression and related activities. Thus, the
funding expiration date of December 26, 2014 needs to be extended.
Further, as recovery efforts have progressed, several stakeholders have determined that
more time is needed to address the impacts of the West Fork Fire Complex sufficiently. The Rio
Grande Watershed Emergency Action Coordination Team (RWEACT), which includes
representatives from Hinsdale, Mineral and Rio Grande Counties, have devised an action plan
for use of these funds. This plan requires that the funds previously set aside in the Disaster
Emergency Fund remain available until June 1, 2015. Accordingly, the Board of Commissioners
from Mineral County, Hinsdale County, Rio Grande County, as well as RWEACT, requested an
extension until that date. Finding good cause, I hereby make the following declarations and
directives relating to the funding of the West Fork Fire Complex recovery efforts.
Il.

of Fire Prevention and Control and the Division of Homeland Security and
Emergency Management are authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the
appropriate resources as may be appropriate and permitted by law.
B. The last sentence of Paragraph I|(E) of Executive Order D 2013-017 is hereby
replaced to read as follows: "These funds shall remain available for this purpose
until June 30, 2016, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster
Emergency Fund."

expired shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive Order
which amends paragraphs I|(C), (D), and (E) of Executive Order D 2013-017, shall remain in
effect until June 30, 2016, unless extended by further Executive Order.

Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire." C.R.S.
§ 24-33.5-703(3).
The Waldo Canyon Fire killed two persons and destroyed 347 homes, and subsequent post-
wildfire flooding caused further damage to homes and infrastructure. I and the Lieutenant
Governor issued a series of executive orders to assist with fighting the fire and to provide
necessary resources for the recovery efforts. Executive Order D 2012-020 provided $4,000,000
for suppression of the Waldo Canyon Fire. Executive Order D 2012-024 authorized use of the •
National Guard to fight the Waldo Canyon Fire and enforce the laws of Colorado. Executive
Order D 2012-031 provided a new total of $6,175,000 for the fire suppression, response, and
recovery efforts related to the Waldo Canyon Fire. Executive Order D 2012-048 provided an
additional $195,000 for disaster recovery resources and extended the time period to use the
encumbered funds to May 2, 2014.

Due to the number and size of this and other fires receiving federal and/or state declarations,
the Division of Fire Prevention and Control needs approximately thirty-six (36) months to
process all contractor payments and close out any Fire Management Assistance Grants with the
Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
In September 2013, Colorado experienced catastrophic flooding, receiving a Stafford Act
disaster declaration with many federal disaster programs implemented. During 2014, Colorado
received Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Community Development Block Grant -
Disaster Relief (CDBG-DR) authorization and funding. The authorization and funding included
any Stafford Act disaster declaration in Colorado during the three years prior to September
2013. Thus CDBG-DR funds are available to assist with the Waldo Canyon Fire recovery. The
Waldo Canyon Fire also received FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) funding,
which may be also be used for flood mitigation projects. Due to receipt of the CDBG-DR funds
and ability of HMGP funds to be used for flood mitigation, the Division of Homeland Security
and Emergency Management (DHSEM) recommended that the state participate in the 25%
non-federal share of the HMGP in the same manner as the Public Assistance (PA) program for
the September 2013 Flood Stafford Act Declaration.
In consultation with the Colorado Recovery Office, I concur with DHSEM's recommendation.
Accordingly, this Executive Order provides funding for half of the 25% non-federal share and
extends the funds in this and previous Executive Orders for an additional sixty (60) months.

Implementing the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2015 and Designating Moneys
in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund for Wildfire Preparedness Activities
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S.
§ 24-33.5-1227(1)(b), I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue
this Executive Order implementing the 2015 Wildfire Preparedness Plan and designating
moneys in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund for wildfire preparedness activities.
Background and Purpose
The Director ("Director") of the Division of Fire Prevention and Control ("Division") is
required to develop an annual Wildfire Preparedness Plan in collaboration with the County
Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State Fire Chiefs' Association, the Director of the Office of
Emergency Management, and the Adjutant General. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1227(2)(a).
The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall be designed to address the following:
(1) The amount of aerial firefighting resources necessary for the State of Colorado at
times of high and low wildfire risk;
(2) The availability of appropriate aerial firefighting equipment and personnel at
times of high fire risk to respond to a wildfire;
(3) The availability of state wildfire engines and staffing of the engines at different
levels of wildfire risk;
(4) The availability of wildfire hand crews, including state inmate wildfire hand
crews, at different levels of wildfire risk; and
(5) A process for ordering and dispatching aerial firefighting equipment and
personnel that is consistent with, and supportive of, the statewide all-hazards
resource mobilization plan prepared pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2015-003
May 15, 2015
Page 2 of 3
The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall also provide recommendations on the use of the
Wildfire Preparedness Fund created in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1227(1)(a).
The Director prepared a draft of the Wildfire Preparedness Plan on March 26, 2015, which
was to be submitted to the Governor and the Members of the General Assembly pursuant to
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1227(b). However, the draft could not be finalized because the Advisory
Committee on Wildland Fire and Prescribed Fire Matters ("Advisory Committee") did not meet
in March due to the absence of a quorum. The Director submitted a finalized plan to the
Advisory Committee at its next regularly scheduled meeting on April 23, 2015. The Advisory
Committee adopted the plan, and the Director submitted it to the Governor and Members of
the General Assembly on April 30, 2014. The Wildfire Preparedness Plan reflects the
collaboration of the County Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State Fire Chiefs' Association, the
Director of the Office of Emergency Management, and the Adjutant General.
Il.
Declaration and Directives
A. The Division is hereby directed to implement the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for
2015 and carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified therein.
B. The Division shall use the moneys in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund to
implement and carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified in the
2015 Wildfire Preparedness Plan, as is necessary.
Ill.
Duration
This Executive Order shall expire upon issuing an Executive Order or Proclamation
implementing the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2016, or upon rescission by subsequent
Executive Order.

imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire." C.R.S.

6 miles South of the town of Mancos. It immediately threatened the Elk Stream and Elk Spring

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 2, and pursuant to the
relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq., l, John
Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a

Counties. My declaration will enable state agencies to coordinate response efforts and make
resources available for response activities.
Pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 5, and pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-
3-104, I also hereby authorize deploying the Colorado National Guard for the purpose of
responding to the May 2017 snow and heavy rains.
1.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. Pursuant to the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, a disaster is "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire, flood...
storm ...." C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). The Governor may order the deployment of resources in
connection with emergency incidents beyond local capabilities if necessary to protect life. C.R.S
§ 24-33.5-705.4.
Beginning May 17, 2017, a major rain and snow storm moved through the north-central
and northeast areas of the State. The storm continued through May 22, 2017. The National
Weather Service predicted significant amounts of snow along the I-25 corridor from Monument
---PAGE---

June 23, 2017

Hill to the Wyoming border. Because these conditions created an imminent threat of injury, loss
of life, and major property damage, the Director of the Division of Homeland Security and
Emergency Management within the Department of Public Safety directed the State to take
measures to prepare to rescue people who might be stranded in the storm. The State engaged
the National Guard to transport Small Unit Support Vehicles to Longmont and north of
Colorado Springs in the event that the National Guard needed to rescue people. Due to
temperatures remaining higher than expected, the snowfall in the corridor was lower than the
National Weather Service had predicted. Such rescue efforts were therefore not ultimately
necessary.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on May 18, 2017, I verbally declared a disaster emergency
for this event in Jefferson, Boulder, Larimer and Weld Counties and activated the State of
Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency
Operations Plan. I further verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National
Guard to assist with rescues related to the snowstorm in Jefferson, Boulder, Larimer and Weld
Counties.

a. The May 2017 snow and heavy rains and associated impacts constitute a disaster
emergency under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. This Executive Order memorializes my
verbal order of May 18, 2017 declaring a disaster emergency, which shall have the full
force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Order.
b. I hereby activate the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery
Plan, also known as the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and
agencies shall take all necessary actions as well as actions requested by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to the Emergency Support Function
Five Annex of the Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery Plan,
including necessary provision of appropriate staff and equipment.
c. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), I hereby encumber $15,000 from the Disaster
Emergency Fund to pay for the response of this disaster emergency.
d. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), I authorize and direct the Director of the Office
of Emergency Management to allocate the funding to the appropriate government
agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other
mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. These funds shall remain available
for this purpose until sixty (60) months from the date of this Order, and any

coordinate

f. This Executive Order memorializes my verbal order of May 18, 2017 activating the

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 2, and pursuant to the
relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Donna
Lynne, Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order
declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Peak 2 Fire in Summit County, enabling state
agencies to coordinate response and recovery efforts and making resources available for
response activities.
Further, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 5, and pursuant to
C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I also hereby authorize employing the Colorado National Guard for the
purpose of supporting fire suppression efforts and any other supporting needs for which the
Guard has capabilities and available resources for the Peak 2 Fire in Summit County.
I. Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire ...." C.R.S §
24-33.5-703(3).
During the afternoon of July 5, 2017, a fire was reported near Breckenridge in Summit
County. Due to the location of the fire, hot and dry conditions, and proximity to the town of
Breckenridge, local, federal and state responders took immediate action to suppress the fire.
Summit County's Emergency Management Office issued pre-evacuation alerts, and
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2017-018
July 19, 2017
Page 2 of 3
subsequently converted those alerts into evacuation orders. Within hours, fire command staff
requested a Type I federal incident management team because of the complexity of the fire
and risk to lives and property. The fire Incident Command staff requested activation of the
Colorado National Guard to support fire suppression efforts.
At approximately 5:00 pm on July 5, 2017, Governor Hickenlooper verbally declared a
disaster emergency for the Peak 2 Fire and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident
Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency Operations Plan.
He further verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard for
fire suppression efforts and any other supporting needs for which the Guard has capabilities
and available resources for the Peak 2 Fire.
Il. Declarations and Directives
A. The Peak 2 Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S §
24-33.5-701, et seq. Governor Hickenlooper's verbal order of July 5, 2017, declaring a
disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the
full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this order.
B. Because the Peak 2 Fire is confined solely to federal lands, financial responsibility for
response and suppression efforts rests with the federal government. To assure timely
reimbursement to the Colorado National Guard, I authorize payment from the
Wildfire Cost Recovery Fund, managed by the Division of Fire Prevention and Control.
C. I authorize and direct the Division of Fire Prevention and Control to coordinate
application to the federal government for funds available for reimbursement,
including funds expended as authorized in Paragraph IIB. The Division shall use funds
from such federal reimbursements to reimburse the State for expending funds in the
Wildfire Cost Recovery Fund to reimburse the Colorado National Guard.
D. Governor Hickenlooper's verbal orders of July 5, 2017 activating the National Guard,
authorizing the use of National Guard assets for fire suppression efforts and any other
supporting needs for which the Guard has capabilities and available resources are
hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of
law as if they were contained within this order.
---PAGE---

July 19, 2017
Page 3 of 3
Ill.
Duration
This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from July 5, 2017, unless extended further by
Executive Order, except that the funds described in paragraph IIB above shall remain available
for the described purposes for sixty (60) months from the date of this Executive Order.

Calling Certain Elements of the Colorado National Guard to Active Duty to
Assist with Emergency Response Efforts Related to Hurricane Harvey
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution, and C.R.S. § 28-3-
104, 1, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive
Order calling certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to state active duty and
implementing the Emergency Management Assistance Compact to assist Texas with
emergency response efforts related to Hurricane Harvey.
I.
Background and Need
The Southern United States recently suffered one of the worst natural disasters in our
nation's history - Hurricane Harvey. The number of lives lost and the amount of property
damaged has devastated communities in its path. The State of Texas appears to have endured the
most damage from this disaster.
As a party to the Emergency Management Assistance Compact, C.R.S. § 24-60-2901
et seq., the State of Colorado is able to provide assistance to states enduring a disaster
emergency. The State of Texas, also a party to the Compact, requested Colorado to pre-
position emergency equipment and personnel to support search and rescue, transportation, and
evacuation efforts. Texas also requested that Colorado backfill Texas personnel participating
in a mission supporting Aeromedical Evacuation Operations.
By this Order, I call certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to active duty
and direct the Colorado National Guard to respond to Texas's request for assistance.
---PAGE---
I1.
Mission and Scope
A. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, as Commander in Chief of military forces, I hereby
employ and call to active duty certain elements of the Colorado National Guard and
implement the Emergency Management Assistance Compact. The State of Colorado
shall provide support personnel and resources to assist Texas in emergency response
efforts related to Hurricane Harvey.
B. I hereby authorize the Director of the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency
management to encumber $850,000 from the Resource Mobilization Fund, pursuant to
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(6), to pay for the use of the National Guard's deployment
under this Executive Order, which will then be reimbursed by the State of Texas
through the Emergency Management Assistance Compact. These funds shall remain
available for this purpose for twelve months from the date of signature of this
Executive Order.
C. I hereby direct Adjutant General Michael A. Loh of the Colorado National Guard to
immediately coordinate and execute all directives issued by this Executive Order.
D. All verbal orders that I issued in regard to this Order are hereby memorialized by
this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were
contained within this Executive Order.
Ill. Duration
This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended
by Executive Order.

disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property
resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to
fire...." C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3).
B. Late in the afternoon on September 9, 2017, the Craig Interagency Dispatch Center
notified the Division of Fire Prevention and Control of a fire in Moffat County, named

Commander of the Pine Tree Fire believes that lightning caused the fire, though the cause

ranches as well as land under the control of the federal Bureau of Land Management.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 2, and pursuant to the
relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, and in
particular C.R.S § 24-33.5-702(1)(f), 1, Donna Lynne, Lieutenant Governor of the State of
Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order authorizing personnel and equipment from Colorado
to assist with emergency response efforts related to wildland fires in California and, pursuant to
C.R.S. §24-60-2901 et seq., implement the Emergency Management Assistance Compact.
I.
Background and Need
California experienced a wildland fire outbreak that killed more than 40 people,
destroyed thousands of homes, burned over 200,000 acres, and required over 11,000 firefighters
and their equipment to battle the fires.
As a party to the Emergency Management Assistance Compact, C.R.S. § 24-60-2901 et
seq., the State of Colorado is able to provide assistance to states and certain United States
Territories enduring a disaster emergency. The State of California, also a party to the Compact,
requested Colorado personnel and equipment, including wildland fire capable engines, to support
the needs of California to respond to wildland fires and provide for the health and safety of
citizens.
By this Order, I authorize personnel and equipment from Colorado to respond to
California's request for assistance.
---PAGE---

October 20, 2017
Page 2 of 2
II. Mission and Scope
A. Pursuant to C.R.S § 24-33.5-702(1)(f), as acting Governor of the State of Colorado,
I hereby authorize personnel and equipment from Colorado to assist with
emergency response efforts related to wildland fires.
B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-60-2901 et seq., I hereby implement the Emergency
Management Assistance Compact. The State of Colorado shall provide personnel
and equipment to assist California in emergency response efforts related to wildland
fires.
C. Due to the current insufficiency of funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund necessary
to pay for the fully-reimbursable expenses for personnel and equipment under the
Emergency Management Assistance Compact, I order the transfer of $2,000,000
from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund into the Disaster Emergency Fund
pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b). I further encumber $2,000,000 in the
Disaster Emergency Fund to pay for the use of personnel and equipment under this
Executive Order, which will then be reimbursed by California through the
Emergency Management Assistance Compact. These funds shall remain available
for this purpose for twelve (12) months from the date of signature of this Executive
Order.
IV. Duration
This Executive Order shall expire 30 days from its date of signature unless
extended by Executive Order, except that the funds described in paragraph I! C above
shall remain available for the described purposes for 12 months from the date of this
Executive Order.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the rclevant
portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W.
Flickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a
state of disaster emergency in La Plata and San Juan Countics duc to the 416 Fire in La Plata
County ("416 Fire"), enabling state agencies to coordinate response and recovery efforts, and
making resources available for response and expenses to state agencies for recovery activities.
Pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and pursuant to C.R.S.
§ 28-3-104, I also herby authorize deploying the Colorado National Guard for the purpose of
responding to the 416 Firc.
I. Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and pcople presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from
any natural causc or causc of human origin, including but not limited to fire." C.R.S § 24-33.5-
703(3).
On June 1, 2018, under red flag conditions for fire danger, a fire of unknown cause
started in La Plata County along U.S. Route 550 between Durango and Silverton. The fire
originated on United States Forest Service property, and the United States Forest Service
assumed responsibility for costs. La Plata County declared a local disaster emergency at
approximately 6:00 PM, on June 1, 2018.
At approximately 8:15 AM on Junc 3, 2018, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for
wildland fire in La Plata County and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident
Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency Opcrations Plan. I further
verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard for wildland fire

reimbursement and to coordinate application for any other funds available related to

Declaring a Disaster Emergency in Las Animas County Due to the Emery Gap Fire
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant
portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, el seq., I, John W.
Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a
state of disaster emergency due to the Emery Gap Fire in Las Animas County ("Emery Gap
Fire"), enabling state agencies to coordinate response and recovery efforts, and making resources
available for response and recovery activities.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from
any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire." C.R.S § 24-33.5-
703(3).
On June 8, 2018, lightning started the Emery Gap Fire on private land in New Mexico,
and the fire crossed into Colorado south of Branson, in Las Animas County. The fire was
estimated to be 1,034 total acres, with 666 acres burned in Colorado. The fire threatened two
structures in Colorado and had the potential to spread further, placing additional property at risk.
The fire exceeded the fire suppression capacity of the local fire agencies.
At approximately 6:00 PM on June 10. 2018. the Division of Fire Prevention and Control
determined the Emery Gap Fire qualified for funding from the Emergency Fire Fund.
---PAGE---

June 28, 2018
Page 2 of 3
At approximately 9:00 PM on June 10. 2018, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for
wildland fire in Las Animas County and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident
Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency Operations Plan.
I. Declarations and Directives
A. The Emery Gap Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under
C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et sey. My verbal order of June 10, 2018, declaring a disaster
emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full
force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order.
B. The State of Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery Plan, also known
as the State Emergency Operations Plan, is hereby activated. All State departments
and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the
Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to the
Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the Colorado Hazard and Incident Response
and Recovery Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as
necessary.
C. The remaining funds in the Emergency Fire Fund are expected to be insufficient to
pay for fire suppression efforts related to the Emery Gap Fire. Upon exhaustion of
those funds, the Disaster Emergency Fund shall be used as an additional funding
source. Accordingly, pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(a). I order two hundred
and fifty thousand dollars ($250,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund be encumbered
to pay for fire suppression and response efforts related to the Emery Gap Fire since
June 8, 2018.
D. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of
Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to
the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute
awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to affect the allocation of the funds.
These funds shall remain available for this purpose until sixty (60) months from the
date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall be reimbursed to
accounts from which they were originally transferred.
E. The Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management is authorized and
directed to coordinate with the Division of Fire Prevention and Control to seck any
available reimbursement from the federal government and the State of New Mexico
for fire suppression and related activities.

Amending Executive Order D 2013 022 to Extend the Availability of Existing Funds
for the West Fork Fire Complex in Mineral, Rio Grande, and Hinsdale Counties
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act. C.R.S.
$ 24-33.5-701, et seg., 1, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue
this Executive Order amending Executive Order D 2013 022 to extend the availability of existing
funds for the West Fork Fire Complex in Mineral, Rio Grande, and Hindale Counties ("West
Fork Fire").
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by
disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as
"the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to
fire, flood [and] water contamination ...." C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3).
On June 5, 2013, lightning started the West Fork Fire in the San Juan National Forest in
Mineral County. By June 23, 2013, the West Fork Fire had grown to over 109,000 acres. On
June 26, 2013, I was traveling outside of the State of Colorado, and Lieutenant Governor Joseph
A. Garcia declared a disaster emergency and made resources available for fire suppression,
response, and recovery efforts in Executive Order D 2013 017.
In Executive Order D 2013 022, I reauthorized the state of disaster emergency for the
West Fork Fire and ordered that two million five hundred thousand dollars ($2,500,000) from the
Colorado Water Conservation Board's Severance Tax Trust Fund Perpetual Base Account be
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2018 004
June 28.2018
Page 2 of2
utilized to help protect communities and natural resources in the West Fork Fire burn area from
post-wildfire dangers.
Due to the need for coordination among county governments and other partners, as well
as the need to secure additional funding, a project to install permanent radar for weather and
stream forecasting will not be complete by July 25, 2018, the date the funding expires per
D 2013 022. This Executive Order therefore extends the availability of the $2,500,000 from the
Colorado Water Conservation Board's Severance Tax Trust Fund Perpetual Base Account to
December 31, 2018, in order to provide adequate time for remaining recovery and protection
efforts in connection with the West Fork Fire.
Amendment
Section II(M) of Executive Order D 2013 022 (which itself amends Executive Order
D 2013 017) is amended to read as follows:
The funds described in paragraph II (J) shall be available until December
31, 2018. The Executive Director of Department of Natural Resources or
his designee shall have the authority to determine when relief efforts have
been completed. Upon this determination, or on January 1, 2019. or as
soon as practicable thereafter, any remaining funds shall be returned to the
Colorado Water Conservation Board's Severance Tax Trust Fund
Perpetual Base Account.
III. Duration
This Executive Order shall remain in effect until rescinded or modified by Executive
Order. In all other respects, Executive Order D 2013 022 shall remain in full force and effect as
originally promulgated.

of June. 2018.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant
portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seg., I, Donna Lynne,
Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state
of disaster emergency due to the Spring Creek Fire in Costilla and Huerfano Counties (the
"Spring Creek Fire"), enabling state agencies to coordinate response and recovery efforts, and
making resources available to state agencies for response and recovery activities.
I.
Background and Purposc
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by
disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as
"the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to
fire." C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3).
The Spring Creek Fire started on June 27, 2018, in Costilla County. The fire spread into
Huerfano County, and is estimated to be 107,967 acres with seventy-seven percent containment
as of July 10, 2018. The fire is primarily on state and private land. Approximately 3,500 homes
were initially evacuated because of the fire. The fire also threatens utilities and a railroad in the
arca. The fire has potential to spread further and impact additional values.
At approximately 6:45 PM on June 27, 2018, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control
determined that the Spring Creek Fire qualified for funds from the Emergency Fire Fund.
---PAGE---

July 11, 2018
Page 2 of 3
At approximately 6:50 PM on June 27, 2018, Governor Hickenlooper verbally declared a
disaster emergency for the Spring Creek Fire and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and
Incident Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency Operations Plan.
Both the Costilla County Board of County Commissioners and the Huerfano County
Board of County Commissioners declared local disaster emergencies due to the Spring Creek
Fire in the late evening of June 27, 2018, and the morning of June 29, 2018, respectively.
Because of the severity of the fire and additional private and state properties at risk, the
Division of Fire Prevention and Control requested a federal Fire Management Assistance Grant
from the Federal Emergency Management Agency at approximately 11:00 PM on June 27, 2018.
The request for a Fire Management Assislance Grant was approved by the Federal Emergency
Management Agency's Regional Administrator at approximately 12:55 PM on June 28, 2018.
Il. Declarations and Directives
A. The Spring Creck Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency
under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. Governor Hickenlooper's verbal order of June
27, 2018, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this
Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were
contained within this Executive Order.
B.
The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments
and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the
Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to
the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and
equipment as necessary.
C.
Due to the insufficiency of funds in both the Emergency Fire Fund and the
Disaster Emergency Fund established in C.R.S § 24-33.5-706(2)(a) to pay for the
State's share of fire suppression and recovery efforts related to the Spring Creek
Fire, I order the transfer of eighteen million dollars ($18,000,000) from the
Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund into the Disaster Emergency Fund pursuant lo
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b). I further encumber eighteen million dollars
($18,000,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund to pay for the fire suppression and
recovery efforts related to the Spring Creek Fire since June 27, 2018. In order to
ensure timely reimbursement to responding agencies, I further encumber and
authorize payment of an additional fifteen million dollars ($15,000,000) from the
Wildfire Cost Recovery Fund, managed by the Division of Fire Prevention and
Control, to cover reimbursable response costs.
