Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending my
earlier declaration of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in Boulder County,
Colorado and extending availability of funds and authorization to enter upon land to
remove debris.
1. Background and Purpose
On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile
Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. As I observed first-
hand the day after the fire began, the Fourmile Fire poses an imminent danger to human
life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster. In response to this disaster, on
September 7, 2010, I issued Executive Order D 2010-012 declaring a disaster emergency.
Two days later, on September 9, 2010, I issued Executive Order D 2010-013, reaffirming
my disaster declaration and making additional state resources available to support the
State's response to the Fourmile Fire.
By the time the Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had
spread to more than 3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and
destroyed 169 homes. With the assistance of Boulder County Emergency Management,
the residents have been diligently working to clear land of fire debris. However, the
inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has
hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This
remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to
public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term.
Once a disaster declaration has been made, state law authorizes the Governor to order the
removal or clearance of debris or wreckage from public or private lands through the use
of "any of the state's instrumentalities" when such debris "may threaten public health or
safety or public or private property." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-002
January 8, 2011
Page 2 of 3
this authority, the local government must "first present[] an unconditional authorization
for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the
case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree|] to indemnify
the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32-
2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required
authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, I issued Executive
Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the state, to
remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property. Although that
executive order expires today, the debris removal efforts are not complete. Indeed, such
efforts are not expected to be complete until sometime in the spring. Thus, I am
extending the debris authorization removal authority. By statute, however, in order to
authorize debris removal I must also declare a disaster emergency and the duration of a
limited to thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration.
Therefore, with the executive order, I will extend the disaster declaration and debris
removal authorization by thirty days, but it expected that several further extensions will
be necessary before the work is completed.
Paragraph I|(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 made $200,000 available for response
and recovery efforts. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund
a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the
position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. The funds from
Executive Order D 2010-2013, however, are only available through September 9, 2011.
In order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, 1 am extending the
availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through
September 20, 2012.
II. Declaration and Directives
In addition to the declarations and directives contained in Executive Orders D 2010-012,
D 2010-013, and 2010-019, I declare and direct, as follows:
A. I hereby declare that Fourmile Fire continues to constitutes a disaster
emergency for purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103.
B.
I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State,
to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile
Fire from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I
acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented
to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or
wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of
debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the
state government against any claim arising from such removal.
C.
The $200,000 encumbered pursuant to paragraph II(B) of Executive Order
D 2010-013 shall remain available through September 30, 2012 for the
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-002
January 8, 2011
Page 3 of 3
purposes of the original encumbrance. Specifically, these funds may be
used to pay for resources as requested by Boulder County or appropriate
state agencies and as approved by the Director of the Division of
Emergency Management to assist with government costs incurred during
the current disaster emergency by government entities, including costs
incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of government entities.
The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is
hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate
agencies. These funds shall remain available for this purpose through
September 20, 2012, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the
Disaster Emergency Fund.
III. Duration
Executive Order D 2010-012 remains in full force and effect as originally promulgated.
The funds made available pursuant to paragraph II(B) of D 2010-013 shall remain
available until September 30, 2012, and in all other respects Executive Order D 2010-013
shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive Order
shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended further by Executive
Order.

Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat Posed by Flooding as
a Result of the Fourmile Fire in Boulder County
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
paris: 2- an eat prion of the Coper do in me state or 9a,.
hereby issues this Executive Order declaring a disaster emergency due to the imminent
threat posed by flooding as a result of the wildfire in Fourmile Canyon in Boulder
County, Colorado.
I. Background and Purpose
On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile
Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. By the time the
Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had spread to more than
3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and destroyed 169
homes.
In response to this disaster, Governor Ritter issued Executive Orders D 2010-012
declaring a disaster emergency and Executive Orders D 2010-013, D 2010-019, and
D 2011-002, reaffirming his disaster declaration and making additional state resources
available. In addition, Governor Hickenlooper issued Executive Orders D 2011-006 and
D 2011-007, reaffirming the disaster declaration and making additional State resources
available to support the State's response to the Fourmile Fire.
The wildfire stripped the burn area of vegetative groundcover and, as a result, according
to the U.S. Geological Survey, the potential for sudden and destructive flooding and
debris flow is dramatically increased. The Fourmile Emergency Stabilization Team
recommends distributing groundcover on the severely burned areas in order to promote
re-vegetation and to minimize erosion and debris flow during spring and summer rains.
Due to steep terrain in the burn area, aerial distribution of mulch is necessary. By letter
dated March 18, 2011, Boulder County requested an executive order from the Governor.
The request included Boulder County's legal analysis and conclusion that,
notwithstanding statutes authorizing county health department nuisance abatement and
local disaster emergency declarations, Boulder County lacks authority to authorize aerial
mulching in the Fourmile Fire burn area.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-009
April 4, 2011
Page 2 of 3
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. C.R.S. § 24-32-2104(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992,
defines a disaster as "the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage,
injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human
origin, including but not limited to fire, flood, ... wind, storm, ... or other water
contamination requiring emergency action to avert danger or damage...." C.R.S. § 24-
32-2103(1.5). Upon a rain event over the burn area, the rate of water discharge will be
significantly greater than under pre-fire conditions and will produce destructive flooding
and debris flow without established groundcover. The threat of spring rains in Boulder
County is imminent and the proximity of burn area creeks to state lands, the city of
Boulder, and residences in Fourmile Canyon means an imminent threat to life and
property exists and, therefore, constitutes a disaster for the purposes of the Act.
II. Declaration and Directives
In addition to the declarations and directives contained in Executive Orders D 2010-012,
D 2010-013, D 2010-019, D 2011-002, D 2011-006, and D 2011-007, 1 declare and direct
as follows:
A.
Flooding as a result of the Fourmile Fire constitutes an imminent threat to
life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster emergency under
C.R.S. § 24-32-2103.
B.
C.
Distributing groundcover by aerial means (aerial mulching) is necessary in
order to attempt to address this disaster emergency. Due to the
unpredictable timing of precipitation events, aerial mulching may not
prevent flooding but early spring distribution offers the highest protection
available given current soil conditions.
Boulder County has received the express consent for aerial mulching of all
but 7 of the approximately 325 affected private property owners in the
Fourmile Fire burn area.
D.
Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2104(7)(b), Boulder County, as a political
subdivision of the state, is directed to utilize available aerial mulching
resources on public and private lands in the Fourmile Fire burn area as
they are reasonably necessary to cope with this disaster emergency.
E.
The aerial mulching effort will expend no State funds and will be
conducted using federal funding from the U.S. Department of Agriculture,
Natural Resources Conservation Service. Specifically, these funds will be
used by Boulder County to contract for aerial mulching in the Fourmile
Fire burn area.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-009
April 4, 2011
Page 3 of 3
III. Duration
Executive Orders D 2010-012, D 2010-013, D 2010-019, D 2011-002, D 2011-006, and
D 2011-007 remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive
Order shall expire 30 days from its date of signature unless extended further by Executive
Order.
GIVEN under my hand and the
Executive Seal of the State of
Colorado this fourth day of
April, 2011.

Governor

EXECUTIVE ORDER

Indian Gulch Fire in Jefferson County
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992,
C.R.S. § 24-32-2100, et seq., John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado,
hereby issues this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the
wildfire in Jefferson County, Colorado.
I. Background and Purpose
On Sunday, March 20, 2011, a wildfire ("Indian Gulch Fire") broke out west of Golden
in Jefferson County in between Golden Gate and Clear Creek Canyons. As of the
morning of March 24th, the fire has spread to more than 1,500 acres, including state and
private lands. Over 280 homes are currently threatened as well as several area
businesses. In addition, gusty winds and dry weather threaten to exacerbate the fire.
Because of the fire's proximity to state lands, the city of Golden, and residences in
Golden Gate Canyon, an aggressive response is essential. Approximately 37 agencies,
including the Colorado State Forest Service, the U.S. Forest Service and local emergency
teams, have responded to the wildfire by deploying a variety of resources, including
approximately 290 firefighters, 30 engines, two air tankers and three helicopters.
Additionally, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's Federal Emergency
Management Agency ("FEMA") has authorized the use of federal funds to help with
firefighting costs. FEMA's authorization makes federal funding available to reimburse
seventy-five percent of the state's eligible firefighting costs under an approved grant for
responding to and controlling designated fires.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, defines a disaster as "the
occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not
limited to ... fire." C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). The Indian Gulch Fire's proximity to
state lands, the city of Golden, and residences in Golden Gate Canyon pose an imminent
danger to life and property and, therefore, constitute a disaster for the purposes of the
Act.

March 24, 2011

B.

State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be
equired and requested by the Director of the Division of Emergency
Management or the Colorado State Forest Service, including provision of
appropriate staff and equipment as necessary.
Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, the funds in the Disaster Emergency
Fund are hereby found insufficient; therefore, pursuant to Section 1
(2)(b)(I) of Ch. 453, Session Laws of Colorado 2010, it is ordered that
$1,500,000 be transferred from the Major Medical Insurance Fund to the
Disaster Emergency Fund. It is further ordered that up to $1,500,000 from
the Disaster Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for the response and
recovery efforts related to the Indian Gulch Fire since its inception. The

reimbursement and to coordinate application for any other funds available
related to this disaster emergency.

Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order
extending an earlier declaration of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in
Boulder County, Colorado and extending availability of funds and authorization to enter
upon land to remove debris.
1. Background and Purpose
On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile
Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. The Fourmile Fire
poses an imminent danger to human life and property and, therefore, constitutes a
disaster. In response to this disaster, on September 7, 2010, Governor Ritter issued
Executive Order D 2010-012 declaring a disaster emergency. Two days later, on
September 9, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-013, reaffirming his
disaster declaration and making additional state resources available to support the State's
response to the Fourmile Fire.
By the time the Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had
spread to more than 3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and
destroyed 169 homes. With the assistance of Boulder County Emergency Management,
the residents have been diligently working to clear land of fire debris. However, the
inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has
hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This
remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to
public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term.
Once a disaster declaration has been made, state law authorizes the Governor to order the
removal or clearance of debris or wreckage from public or private lands through the use
of "any of the state's instrumentalities" when such debris "may threaten public health or
safety or public or private property." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-013
May 6, 2011
Page 2 of 3
this authority, the local government must "first present [] an unconditional authorization
for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the
case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree|] to indemnify
the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32-
2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required
authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, Governor Ritter
issued Executive Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality
of the state, to remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property.
On April 7, 2011, I issued Executive Order D 2011-012, which once again provided 30
additional days of authorization to remove debris. Although that executive order expires
today, the debris removal efforts are not complete. Indeed, such efforts are not expected
to be complete until sometime in the spring. Thus, I am extending the debris
authorization removal authority. By statute, however, in order to authorize debris
removal I must also declare a disaster emergency, the duration of which is limited to
thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration. Therefore, with
the executive order, I will extend the disaster declaration and debris removal
authorization by thirty days, but it expected that several further extensions will be
necessary before the work is completed.
Paragraph II(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 made $200,000 available for response
and recovery efforts. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund
a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the
position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. The funds from
Executive Order D 2010-2013, however, are only available through September 9, 2011.
In order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, I am extending the
availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through
September 20, 2012.
II. Declaration and Directives

D 2010-013, 2010-019, Executive Order D 2011-002, Executive Order D 2011-006,
Executive Order D 2011-007, and Executive Order D 2011-012, I declare and direct, as
follows:
A.
I hereby declare that Fourmile Fire continues to constitutes a disaster
emergency for purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103.
B.
I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State,
to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile
Fire from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I
acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented
to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or
wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of
---PAGE---

May 6, 2011
Page 3 of 3
debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the
state government against any claim arising from such removal.
C.
The $200,000 encumbered pursuant to paragraph II(B) of Executive Order
D 2010-013 shall remain available through September 30, 2012 for the
purposes of the original encumbrance. Specifically, these funds may be
used to pay for resources as requested by Boulder County or appropriate
state agencies and as approved by the Director of the Division of

incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of government entities.
The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is

available until September 30, 2012, and in all other respects Executive Order D 2010-013
shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive Order

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and

Background and Purpose
Nebraska has experienced and is expecting significant rising waters in the Platte River
Basin which will likely cause significant flooding, property damage and potential danger
to citizens. The Governor of Nebraska has declared a state disaster and has validated to
the State of Colorado that Nebraska is threatened by that emergency disaster. In order to
mitigate the threat of flooding, Nebraska is undertaking sandbagging operations and
requires the support of a UH-60 helicopter, pilot, and crew chief in the North Platte,
Nebraska area.
On June 4', 2011 the State of Nebraska filed with the State of Colorado an EMAC "Form
REQ A, 2011" requesting said resources by June 7'", 2011, to be released June 12'h,
2011.
I find that the conditions under which such resources can be made available and used to
meet the emergency needs of the State of Nebraska under the EMAC have been satisfied
as a result of the occurrence and imminent threat of emergency disaster described above.

A. The State of Nebraska has communicated that it is experiencing an emergency
disaster occurring within that state which provides a basis for activation of the
EMAC, and has requested certain resources from the State of Colorado,
including certain air assets of the Colorado National Guard.

Consistent with the EMAC and under my authority as the Commander in
Chief of the Colorado National Guard, Colo. Const., sec. 5, I hereby authorize

emergency disaster, as requested by the Director of the Colorado Division of

reimbursed by the State of Nebraska.

Shell Fire Complex in Las Animas County
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
articular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992
C.R.S. § 24-32-2100, et seq., John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado
hereby issues this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the
wildfires in Las Animas County, Colorado.
1. Background and Purpose
On Tuesday, June 7, 2011, two wildfires ("Shell Fire" and "Brice Fire") were reported on
private land in Las Animas County. As of the evening of June 8, the fires had spread to
approximately 9,000 acres on private lands. Immediate threat is to 200 ranch homes and
structures, state highway 109, and a microwave tower. Two additional wildfires started
on June 7 to the west of the Shell and Brice fires on federal land. On June 12, a fifth fire
(Mesa de Maya Fire") was reported southwest of the town of Kim. Predicted hot
weather and strong gusty winds coupled with abundant dry fuels indicate an aggressive
response is essential. Las Animas County resources have been fully engaged in fighting
the wildfires which have now exceeded their management capacity. Approximately nine
federal and state agencies, including the Colorado State Forest Service, the U.S. Forest
Service, Bureau of Land Management, Department of Defense, Division of Emergency
Management, Department of Corrections, adjacent counties, and local emergency teams
have responded to the wildfire by deploying a variety of resources, including over 200
firefighters, three engines, four bulldozers, two single engine air tankers, and two
helicopters. Together, the Shell, Brice, and Mesa de Maya Fires will be managed under
one command structure utilizing and sharing resources among the three fires and be
known as the "Shell Fire Complex."
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992 defines a disaster as "the
occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or
property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not
limited to ... fire." C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). The Shell Fire Complex's proximity to
ranch headquarters, the town of Kim, and state highway 109 pose an imminent danger to
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-022
July 19, 2011
Page 2 of 3
life and property and, therefore, constitute a disaster for the purposes of the Act. In
response to this disaster, on June 9, 2011, I declared a disaster emergency.
Il.

A.
B.
C.
D.
The Shell Fire Complex hereby constitutes a disaster emergency for
purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103. My verbal order of June 9, 2011,
declaring a state disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this
Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were
contained within this Executive Order.
The State Emergency Operations Plan ("Plan") is hereby activated. All
State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be
required and requested by the Director of the Division of Emergency
Management or the Colorado State Forest Service, including provision of
appropriate staff and equipment as necessary.
Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, the funds in the Disaster Emergency
Fund are hereby found insufficient; therefore, consistent with Section 1,
Subsection (2)(b)(I) of Ch. 453, Session Laws of Colorado 2010, it is
ordered that $1,100,000 be transferred from the Major Medical Insurance
Fund to the Disaster Emergency Fund. It is further ordered that up to
$1,100,000 from the Disaster Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for
the response and recovery effort related to the Shell Fire Complex since its
inception. The Colorado State Forester is hereby authorized and directed
to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies. These
funds shall remain available for this purpose for one year from the date of
this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the
Disaster Emergency Fund.
The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management and the
Colorado State Forest Service are authorized and directed to coordinate
application to the federal government for funds available for
reimbursement and to coordinate application for any other funds available
related to this disaster emergency.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992,
C.R.S. § 24-32-2100, et seq., and specifically C.R.S. § 24-32-2505, I. John W.
Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order
extending an earlier declaration of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in
Boulder County, Colorado and extending availability of funds and authorization to enter
upon land to remove debris.
Background and Purpose
On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile
Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. The Fourmile Fire
poses an imminent danger to human life and property and, therefore, constitutes a
disaster. In response to this disaster, on September 7, 2010, Governor Ritter issued
Executive Order D 2010-012 declaring a disaster emergency. Two days later, on
September 9, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-013. reaffirming his
disaster declaration and making additional state resources available to support the State's
response to the Fourmile Fire.
By the time the Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had
spread to more than 3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and
destroyed 169 homes. With the assistance of Boulder County Emergency Management,
the residents have been diligently working to clear land of fire debris. However, the
inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has
hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This
remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to
public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term.
Once a disaster declaration has been made, state law authorizes the Governor to order the
removal or clearance of debris or wreckage from public or private lands through the use
of "any of the state's instrumentalities" when such debris "may threaten public health or
---PAGE---

July 27, 2011
Page 2 of 3
safety or public or private property." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke
this authority, the local government must "first present|] an unconditional authorization
for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the
case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree|| to indemnify
the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32--
2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required
authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, Governor Ritter
issued Executive Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality
of the state, to remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property. I
issued Executive Order D 2011-013 and Executive Order D 2011-017, which provided
additional thirty-day extensions of authorization to remove debris. The debris removal
efforts are still not complete. Indeed, such efforts are not expected to be complete until
November 2011. I understand that after September 30, 2011, Boulder County will begin
mandatory debris removal procedures on private properties that have not complied with
previous debris removal requests and offers of assistance. Thus, I am extending the
debris authorization removal authority again. By statute, however, in order to authorize
debris removal I must also declare a disaster emergency, the duration of which is limited
to thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration. Therefore,
with this executive order, I will extend the disaster declaration and debris removal
authorization by thirty days, but it is expected that further extensions will be necessary
before the work is completed.
Paragraph I|(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 made $200,000 available for response
and recovery efforts. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund
a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the
position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. The funds from
Executive Order D 2010-013, however, are only available through September 9, 2011. In
order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, I am extending the
availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through
September 20, 2012.
Declaration and Directives
In addition to the declarations and directives contained in Executive Orders D 2010-012,
D 2010-013. and D 2010-019, Executive Order D 2011-002, Executive Order D 2011-
006, Executive Order D 2011-007, Executive Order D 2011-012, Executive Order D 2011-
013, and Executive Order D 2011-017. I declare and direct, as follows:
A.
I hereby declare that Fourmile Fire continues to constitute a disaster
emergency for purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103.
B.
I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State,
to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile
Fire from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I
acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2011-024
July 27, 2011
Page 3 of 3
to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or
wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of
debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the
state government against any claim arising from such removal.
C.
The $200,000 encumbered pursuant to paragraph I|(B) of Executive Order
D 2010-013 shall remain available through September 30, 2012, for the
purposes of the original encumbrance. Specifically, these funds may be
used to pay for resources as requested by Boulder County or appropriate
state agencies and as approved by the Director of the Division of
Emergency Management to assist with government costs incurred during
the current disaster emergency by government entities, including costs
incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of government entities.
The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is
hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate
agencies. These funds shall remain available for this purpose through
September 20, 2012, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the
Disaster Emergency Fund.
III. Duration
Executive Order D 2010-012 remains in full force and effect as originally
promulgated. The funds made available pursuant to paragraph I|(B) of D 2010-013
shall remain available until September 30, 2012, and in all other respects Executive
Order D 2010-013 shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This
Executive Order shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended
further by Executive Order.

Colorado this twenty-seventh day of
July, 2011

Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a
state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in Park County, Colorado.
Background and Purpose
On Sunday, June, 17, 2012, a wildfire ("Springer Fire") started in Park County near Eleven Mile
Canyon. The fire grew rapidly being fueled by extremely dry vegetation, low relative humidity,
high temperatures, and windy conditions. The fire originated on U.S. Forest Service ownership
but private land in the vicinity puts many individuals and private values at risk. As of the
morning of June 18, the fire has spread to approximately 400 acres on federal lands. The
following areas and subdivisions are threatened: Wagon Tongue, Beaver Ranch, Camp
Alexander, 11 mile Campground, Hidden Valley, Echo Valley Forest Glen, Blue Mountain, and
others. Park County and local fire department resources have been fully engaged in fighting the
wildfire in cooperation with the USFS. Predicted hot weather and strong gusty winds coupled
with abundant dry fuels pose a real threat of the fire spreading toward state and private values
at risk and indicate an aggressive response is essential.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, defines a disaster as "the occurrence
or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire." C.R.S. §
24-32-2103(1.5). The Springer Fire's proximity to sub-developments, the town of Lake George,
and 11 Mile State Park poses an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore,
constitutes a disaster for the purposes of the Act. In response to this disaster, on June 17,
2012, I declared a disaster emergency.

B.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Creating StudyColorado within the Department of Higher Education
Pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the authority vested in
the Office of the Governor, I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby
issue this Executive Order creating StudyColorado, a program within the Colorado Department
of Higher Education.
I. Background, Need, and Purpose
International students contribute directly to Colorado's economy and support Colorado
businesses. It is estimated, for the 2010-2011 academic year, that international students and
their dependents contributed almost $165 million in tuition and fees to the Colorado economy,
and a total of over $235 million when living expenses are factored in.
Equally important to the economic impact to the state, international students enrich our
campuses and teach our students to collaborate across cultures and borders. When they return
to their home country, international students become "ambassadors" for Colorado, promoting
our state with family, friends and-later, when they graduate and enter the workforce-
business colleagues. In many cases, international students who have studied in Colorado have
gone on to influential positions in their home countries. Colorado benefits from the
relationships established by these students during their months or years at our institutions.
Colorado's businesses also benefit from international students. The Governor's Trade and
Tourism Ambassador Program (TTAP) was established by Executive Order D2011-004 on
January 11, 2011 to help integrate Colorado into the global economy with the express purpose
of promoting the export of Colorado goods and services to other countries, persuading foreign
investors to establish or expand operations in Colorado, and attracting more tourists to the
state's year-round attractions. TTAP Ambassadors in turn established increasing the number of
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2012-028
July 6, 2012
Page 2 of 4
international students in Colorado as a top priority due to the broad potential impact across all
three areas of exports, foreign investment and tourism.
Many of our institutions of higher education are seeking to diversify their student bodies and
many are actively recruiting international students. As a state, however, Colorado remains well
below average in the number of international students. Similarly, when ranked by the overall
size of the population, Colorado falls short in the number of international students it attracts.
Colorado can add to the efforts of the institutions with a statewide marketing effort that
promotes Colorado as a study destination and leverages the state's trade and tourism activities.
Il. Mission and Scope
The mission of StudyColorado will be to attract international students to Colorado through the
unified outreach efforts of the state, higher education, and the business community.
StudyColorado, with its partners, will engage students to form lifelong connections with
Colorado.
A.
StudyColorado's goals will be to:
i.
ii.
ili.
iv.
Support the international enrollment goals of the state's institutions of
higher education;
Create new economic opportunities for Colorado businesses through the
influx of international students and their families;
Create a more diverse learning environment to help Colorado students be
more competitive in a global workplace; and
Foster lasting relationships between international students and Colorado
that will benefit international trade and investment.
B.
Study Colorado will achieve these goals by, among other activities:
i. Developing a unique state-wide higher education brand and integrating it
into key messaging for state leaders to promote Colorado higher education
internationally;
ii. Providing a forum for exchange of information related to international
education;
ili. Helping to create a welcoming culture for international students and visitors.
In carrying out its activities, StudyColorado will engage with non-profit and other organizations
in Colorado related to target countries including, but not limited to, foreign consulates and
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2012-028
July 6, 2012
Page 3 of 4
country-focused
organizations such as the Canada-Colorado Association, US-Mexico
Foundation, and Japan America Society of Colorado.
IlI. Membership and Board of Directors
A. Membership in StudyColorado will include institutions of higher education that
i. Are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission of the North Central
Association of Colleges and Schools;
ii. Are headquartered in the State of Colorado; and
ili. Support the mission and goals of StudyColorado. Each member institution
shall designate an individual as a representative to StudyColorado.
StudyColorado may have as members other organizations as agreed by its
Board of Directors.
B. StudyColorado will have a Board of Directors, the membership of which will include
but not be limited to:
i. The Executive Director of the Department of Higher Education or his/her
designee;
ii. The Executive Director of the Office of Economic Development and
International Trade or his/her designee;
ili. At least five representatives of higher education institutions selected by a
vote of all higher education member institutions, each for a term of three
years;
iv. At least four representatives from the Colorado business community, who
may include members of the Governor's Trade and Tourism Ambassador
Program, appointed by the Governor, each for a term of three years.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2012-028
July 6, 2012
Page 4 of 4
IV. Staffing and Resources
StudyColorado will be housed within the Colorado Department of Higher Education, which shall
provide necessary administrative support.
StudyColorado shall have the power to accept gifts, grants and donations and to collect fees,
consistent with Colorado law, from institutions of higher education, private entities and
persons for purposes consistent with its mission and goals. Any money contributed to
StudyColorado shall be directed to the Department of Higher Education.
V. Duration
This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the
Governor.
GIVEN under my hand and the
Executive Seal of the State of
Colorado this sixth day of
July, 2012.
ohn W. Hickenloope

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution and relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster
Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-700, et seq., I, Governor John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of
the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order affirming the verbal declaration of a
state of disaster emergency due to wildfires in Rio Blanco County, Colorado.
1.
Background and Purpose
On Thursday, July 19, 2012 and Saturday, July 21, 2012, respectively, two wildfires, the Powell
Fire and the Little Duck Fire (together, the "Powell Complex") started in Rio Blanco County on
lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management. The fires grew rapidly due to extremely
dry vegetation, low relative humidity, high temperatures, and windy conditions. Lightning
strikes are believed to have caused both wildfires. Rio Blanco County and local fire department
resources have been fully engaged in both fighting the wildfires and notifying residents of the
potential need to evacuate. Predicted hot weather and strong gusty winds, coupled with
abundant dry fuels, pose a real threat of putting additional state and private values at risk and
necessitating an aggressive response. A National Type 2 Incident Management Team was
immediately ordered for the Complex. On July 21, 2012, the Colorado Division of Fire
Prevention and Control received a request from the Rio Blanco County Sheriff to assume charge
of the Complex in accord with the Emergency Fire Fund Agreement. The State accepted the
Complex as an Emergency Fire Fund-designated fire and verbally notified the Rio Blanco County
Sheriff at 1353 hours on July 21. As of July 24, the fires had spread to approximately 1,650
acres and are 85% contained.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2012-034
July 24, 2012
Page 2 of 3
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin." C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). The proximity of
the fires in Rio Blanco County to the Strawberry subdivision and historic cow camps, as well as
their proximity to power lines, and mineral extraction infrastructure, poses an imminent danger
to life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster for the purposes of the Act. A disaster
emergency was verbally declared on July 21, 2012.
II.
Declaration and Directives
A. The Powell Complex wildfires in Rio Blanco County constitute a disaster emergency
under C.R.S. 9 24-33.5-703. The verbal order of July 21, 2012, declaring a disaster
emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full
force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order.
B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments
and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the
Director of the Office of Emergency Management, including provision of appropriate
staff and equipment as necessary.
C. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), the funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are
hereby found insufficient to pay for fire suppression efforts related to the Powell
Complex. Therefore, it is ordered that $210,000 be transferred from the Control
Maintenance Trust Fund into the Disaster Emergency Fund. The Director of the
Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the
funding to the appropriate government agencies. These funds shall remain available
for this purpose for one year from the date of this Executive Order, and any
unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund.
D. The Department of Public Safety is authorized and directed to coordinate application
to the federal government for funds available for reimbursement and to coordinate
application for any other funds available related to this disaster emergency.

Declaration of Disaster Emergency Due to Imminent Flood Risk Associated with the
High Park Fire in Larimer County and the Waldo Canyon Fire in El Paso County and
Making Funds Available for Flood Warning
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution and relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster
Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-700, et seq., 1, Governor John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of
the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order reaffirming his earlier declaration of a
state of disaster emergency due to the wildfires and resulting increased flood risk in Larimer
County and El Paso County, Colorado and making additional resources available for flood
warning.
Background and Purpose
The High Park Fire in Larimer County ignited on June 9, 2012 and burned 87,284 acres and
destroyed 259 homes. The Waldo Canyon Fire ignited on June 23, 2012 and burned 18,247
acres and destroyed 346 homes. Inter-agency Burned Area Emergency Response teams
assessed the resulting damage and determined that the burned areas and those areas
surrounding and/or immediately downstream from the burned areas are at much greater flood
risk then prior to the fire. Many of these flood risk areas demand precipitation monitoring,
stream monitoring, and flood warning equipment to address this increased risk.
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by
disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire [or] flood..."
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703 (3). The increased flood risk resulting from both the High Park Fire and the
Waldo Canyon Fire poses an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore, constitutes a
disaster for the purposes of the Act.
---PAGE---

Page 2 of 2
Il.

A.
B.
I hereby declare that the imminent risk of flooding associated with the High Park
and the Waldo Canyon Fires constitutes a disaster emergency for purposes of
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(4).
Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4) the funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are
found to be insufficient to pay for flood warning equipment to address the
increased flood risk. Therefore it is ordered that $200,000 is transferred into the
Disaster Emergency Fund from the Water Quality Improvement Fund in the
Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment. These funds are to be
used as grants of up to $25,000 each to appropriate jurisdictions and agencies in
El Paso and Larimer counties to fund 75% of the cost of precipitation monitoring,
stream monitoring, and flood warning equipment (25% local match). The
Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and
directed to allocate the funding through this grant program to the appropriate
agencies. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for eighteen
months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall
remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund.
III.
Duration
This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended further
by Executive Order, except that the funds described in paragraph I|(B) above shall remain
available for the described purposes for eighteen months from the date of this Executive Order.

Background and Purpose
On October 23, 2012 at approximately 1400 hours, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control
(DFPC) received a request for assistance from the Custer County Sheriff for a wildfire burning
near the town of Wetmore. At the time of the request the fire was threatening approximately
350 homes in and around the Town of Wetmore and mandatory evacuations were in progress.
At least one primary residence and at one other structure had already been destroyed. The
cause of this fire is currently unknown.
At approximately 1515 hours the DFPC Fire Management Officer (FMO) completed his
assessment and determined that the fire met the criteria for an Emergency Fire Fund (EFF) fire.
In addition to the homes and businesses, the fire is also threatening roads, utilities and a
watershed in the area. The current weather conditions were southwest winds 15 to 30 mph
with gusts to 75 mph, relative humidity at 9 percent. The fire had burned approximately 700
acres of private and public land and was 0 percent contained.
Custer County requested transfer of the fire to the State of Colorado under the EFF provisions
and the request was approved by the Governor at 1517 hours.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular,
pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-700, et

Background and Purpose

during calendar years 2010 and 2011. 2011 was the largest amount since calendar year 2003.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in

Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a disaster
emergency due to the Fern Lake Fire in Larimer County and authorizing the National Guard to
assist with fighting the Fern Lake Fire.
Background and Purpose
On October 9, 2012, the Fern Lake Fire started in Rocky Mountain National Park. Early in the
morning hours of December 1, 2012, extreme fire weather conditions caused the fire to more
than double in size from 1,515 acres to over 3,100 acres and begin threatening structures inside
Rocky Mountain National Park and west of the Town of Estes Park in Larimer County. Over 600
evacuation notices were sent to telephone numbers in the evacuation area. Due to the fire
growth on December 1, 2012, firefighters are now deployed to steep, rugged terrain with
limited vehicle access. On December 4, 2012, the Type 1 Incident Management Team managing
this fire requested a Colorado National Guard helicopter for rescue and/or medivac, if
necessary, during this incident. This request was verbally approved at 1109 hours on December
4, 2012. The fire has grown to 3,477 acres, with 1000 structures threatened and 1 structure
destroyed.

A. The Fern Lake Fire constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. §§ 24-33.5-701, 705.
My verbal order of December 4, 2012, authorizing use of the National Guard is hereby
memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if

agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management, including provision of appropriate staff and
equipment as necessary.

Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for the use of the National Guard helicopter.
These funds exist unencumbered in the Disaster Emergency Fund due to unexpended
amounts from previous disasters. The actual cost of the National Guard helicopter and
personnel will be reimbursed to the Disaster Emergency Fund by the U.S. Government.
The Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed
to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and execute awards,
purchase orders or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. These funds
shall remain available for this purpose for eighteen months from the date of this
Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency
Fund.
Ill.

Executive Order, except that the funds described in paragraph I|(C) above shall remain available
for the described purposes for eighteen months from the date of this Executive Order.

Amending Executive Order D 2012-006, Regarding Suspending Prescribed or Controlled Fire
Pending Review of Protocols
Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution, I, John W.
Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order amending
Executive Order D 2012-006.
Background and Purpose
On March 28, 2012, pursuant to Article IV, Section 13, C.R.S. § 23-31-308, based on a finding of
extreme fire danger, we issued Executive Order D 2012-006 suspending prescribed or
controlled fire on state or private lands pending review of agency protocols for prescribed or
controlled fire. The suspension applied to all state lands as well as state agencies that apply
prescribed or controlled fire on non-state lands under contracts or agreements with other
entities. At the time, Colorado was experiencing unseasonably high temperatures and dry
conditions which led to a number of wildfires across the State.
Although weather conditions across Colorado have changed over the recent months, for those
Colorado residents living in the wildland-urban interface, there is still concern of disastrous
wildfire. Slash and burn pile operations in this area will reduce the risk of devastating wildfires,
in addition to helping firefighters control such outbreak when they do occur. These fuel
treatment activities not only reduce wildfire potential, but work to increase the heath of
forests, by thinning forest strands and eliminating weak and diseased trees. Weaker trees that
remain in the forest are prone to insect attacks and disease.
In order to best serve the residents on the wildland-urban interface and promote the health
and wellbeing of our forests, slash pile burning remains the least expensive and most effective
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2013-002
January 30, 2012
Page 2 of 3
method of removing slash. This procedure is conducted with caution and consideration, as
projects are planed months and sometimes years in advance. This Division of Fire Prevention
and Control will work to ensure continued safety and protection for residents on the wildland-
urban interface, while promoting the health and longevity of our State's natural forests through
properly regulated pile burnings.
Declaration and Directives
A. Executive Order D 2012-006 (State-wide suspension on prescribed or controlled
fires) is hereby amended to allow for the resumption of slash pile burnings under
controlled conditions.
B. Slash pile burn operations conducted by state agencies or on state lands shall follow
the new guidelines and procedures established by the Division of Fire Prevention
and Control to ensure that all such burns are conducted in a safe and effective
manner.
C. The Division of Fire Prevention and Control shall observe the following minimum
guidelines for prescribed pile fires:
1. Ignition of piles shall occur only on days when there is adequate snow cover and
the Colorado Air Pollution Control Division has determined that weather
conditions are appropriate for burning because good smoke dispersal can be
achieved;
2. Piles shall be ignited as early in the morning as possible and operations will cease
before sunset;
3. Fire suppression resources shall be on site when piles are burned; and
4. Pile burns shall occur only after proper notification of residents of potentially
affected areas and local government officials.

Page 3 of 3

promulgated.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to article IV, section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 24-33.5-
1226(4)(b) of the Colorado Revised Statutes I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of
Colorado, hereby issues this Executive Order implementing the 2013 Wildfire Preparedness
Plan and designating monies in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund for wildfire preparedness
activities.
Background and Purpose
C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1226(3)(a) requires the Director ("Director") of the Division of Fire
Prevention and Control ("Division") to develop an annual Wildfire Preparedness Plan, in
collaboration with the County Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State Fire Chiefs Association,
the Director of the Office of Emergency Management and the Adjutant General.
The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall be designed to address the following:
(1) The amount of aerial firefighting resources necessary for the state of Colorado at times of
high and low wildfire risk;
(2) The availability of appropriate aerial firefighting equipment and personnel at times of high
fire risk to respond to a wildfire;
(3) The availability of state wildfire engines and staffing of the engines at different levels of
wildfire risk;
(4) The availability of state inmate wildfire hand crews at different levels of wildfire risk; and
(5) A process for ordering and dispatching aerial firefighting equipment and personnel that is
consistent with, and supportive of, the statewide mobilization plan prepared pursuant to
C.R.S. 9 24-33.5-705.4.
The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall also provide recommendations on the use of the
Wildfire Preparedness Fund created in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1226(4)(a).
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2013-008
June 11, 2013
Page 2 of 2
The Director prepared the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2013 as required by law and
submitted it to the Governor and General Assembly on December 20, 2012. The plan was
identified as "Provisional" because the Division had not yet completed the fire aviation plan and
the plan for the staffing of state wildfire engines for 2013.
Subsequently, the Division completed its analysis of the costs of the 2012 fire season,
the financial resources available for the 2013 fire season, and considered the State's
preparedness needs. In collaboration with the County Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State
Fire Chiefs' Association, the Director of the Office of Emergency Management and the Adjutant
General, the Director prepared and submitted a "Final" Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2013 on
March 29, 2013.
Declaration and Directives
A. The Division is hereby directed to implement the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2013
and carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified therein.
B. The Division shall use the monies in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund to implement and
carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified in the 2013 Wildfire
Preparedness Plan, as is necessary.
III.
Duration
This Executive Order shall expire upon issuing an Executive Order or Proclamation
implementing the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2014, or upon rescission by subsequent
Executive Order.

1.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire."
C.R.S. 9 24-33.5-703(3).
On June 11, 2013 at 1256 hours, the Royal Gorge Fire was reported south of the Royal Gorge
Bridge and Arkansas River. This wind-driven fire quickly grew in size and intensity, prompting
the evacuation of 190 homes and subsequently the Colorado Territorial Correctional Facility.
The fire started on the south side of river and spotted to the north side. All available
firefighting resources were committed to firefighting and structural protection.
At approximately 1420 hours the Fremont County Sheriff determined that the fire exceeded the
ability of the county and other local resources to contain and extinguish the fire and requested
transfer of the fire to the State of Colorado under the Emergency Fire Fund (EFF) provisions.
Because the fire was increasing in intensity and rapidly spreading, the Governor's Authorized
Representative (GAR) notified Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) at 1448 hours
that the Royal Gorge fire could threaten such destruction as would constitute a major disaster
and assistance under the Fire Management Assistance Grant (FMAG) Program may be
requested.

June 12, 2013
Page 2 of 3
At 1526 hours the Division of Fire Prevention and Control completed its assessment and
determined that the fire met the criteria for EFF designation. The EFF request was approved by
the Governor at 1530 hours on June 11, 2013.
At 1630 hours the Division of Fire Prevention and Control completed its assessment and
determined that the fire met the criteria for making a request for federal assistance under the
FMAG Program. The GAR submitted the request to FEMA at 1648 hours. FEMA notified the
GAR at 2059 hours that the request was approved.

A. The Royal Gorge Fire constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704.
My order of June 11, 2013 at 1604 hours, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby
memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if
it were contained within this Executive Order.
B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and
agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management, including provision of appropriate staff and
equipment as necessary.
C. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), the funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are
hereby found insufficient to pay for fire suppression efforts related to the Royal Gorge
Fire. Therefore, it is ordered that $4,500,000 be transferred into the Disaster
Emergency Fund from the General Fund appropriation in Fiscal Year 2012-13 to the
Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund. It is further ordered that $4,500,000 from the
Disaster Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for the fire suppression, response, and
recovery effort related to the Royal Gorge Fire since its inception.
Included in the specified amount is $195,000 for recovery related to this disaster. These
funds may be used to pay for disaster recovery resources as approved by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management to assist with state and local government costs
incurred during and as a result of the current disaster emergency, including costs
incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of local government entities. The
Director of the Colorado Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and
directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate agencies and execute awards,
purchase orders or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. These funds
shall remain available for this purpose for eighteen months from the date of this
Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency
Fund.

Executive Order D 2013-009
June 12, 2013
Page 3 of 3
D. My verbal orders activating the National Guard and authorizing the utilization of
National Guard assets to fight the Royal Gorge Fire and enforce the laws of the State of
Colorado as provided in C.R.S. § 28-3-104 are hereby memorialized by this Executive
Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this

E. The Colorado Department of Public Safety is authorized and directed to coordinate

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104, relevant portions of the Colorado
Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., and Colorado Constitution article IV,
Section 13, I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this
Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the East Peak Fire in Huerfano
and Las Animas Counties, Colorado and making resources available to fight the fire and address
the disaster emergency.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire." C.R.S.
§24-33.5-703(3).
On June 19, 2013, shortly before 2000 hours, the East Peak Fire was reported to state
authorities near the Boy Scout Ranch in the Spanish Peaks area of Huerfano County. This wind-
driven fire was quickly growing in size and intensity, prompting the mandatory evacuation of
the Boy Scout Ranch and area homes. All available firefighting resources were committed to
firefighting and structural protection.
At approximately 2100 hours the Huerfano County Sheriff determined that the fire would
exceed the ability of the county and other local resources to contain and extinguish it and
requested the response of the Division of Fire Prevention and Control. The Huerfano County
Sheriff requested transfer of the fire to the State of Colorado under the Emergency Fire Fund
(EFF) provisions. At 2145 hours the Division of Fire Prevention and Control completed its
assessment and determined that the East Peak Fire met the criteria for EFF designation. The EFF
request was approved by the Lieutenant Governor at 2202 hours on June 19, 2013.
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2013-013
June 21, 2013
Page 2 of 4
On June 20, 2013 at approximately 0915 hours, the Huerfano County Sheriff requested National
Guard Helicopters for suppression assistance. The Lieutenant Governor verbally approved this
request and the use of two National Guard Helicopters at approximately 0925 hours.
At approximately 1200 hours, the East Peak Fire extended into Las Animas County. At 1247
hours, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control requested that Las Animas County be added
to the EFF designation. The Governor verbally approved this request at approximately 1319
hours.
On June 20, 2013 by approximately 1300 hours, the fire continued to significantly increase in
size to over 2,000 acres with some structures at the Boy Scout Ranch destroyed and the
evacuation zone increased to east from the Town of La Veta to Interstate 25 and from the City
of Walsenburg south to the Huerfano County line. Based on size up information that the fire
was increasing in intensity and rapidly spreading, the Governor's Authorized Representative
(GAR) notified Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) at approximately 1330 hours
that the East Peak Fire could threaten such destruction as would constitute a major disaster
and assistance under the Fire Management Assistance Grant (FMAG) Program may be
requested.
At approximately 1400 hours the Division of Fire Prevention and Control completed its
assessment and determined that the East Peak Fire met the criteria for making a request for
federal assistance under the FMAG Program and the GAR submitted the request to FEMA.
FEMA notified the GAR on July 21, 2013, at 1259 hours that the request was approved.
At approximately 1540 hours, on July 20, 2013, the Spanish Peaks Regional Medical Center
contacted the Governor's Office and requested approval to move the pharmacy to an alternate
location if the Medical Center evacuated. The Governor verbally approved this request at 1546
hours.
Il.
Declaration and Directives
A. The East Peak Fire constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(4). The
Lieutenant Governor's verbal order of June 19, 2013, at 2202 hours, declaring a disaster
emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force
and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order.
B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and
agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management, including provision of appropriate staff and
equipment as necessary.
---PAGE---

June 21, 2013
Page 3 of 4
C. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), it is ordered that $3,000,000 from the Disaster
Emergency Fund is encumbered to pay for the fire suppression, response, and recovery
effort related to the East Peak Fire since its inception.
Included in the specified amount is $195,000 for recovery related to this disaster. These
funds may be used to pay for disaster recovery resources as approved by the Director of
the Office of Emergency Management to assist with state and local government costs
incurred during and as a result of the current disaster emergency, including costs
incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of local government entities. The
Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to
allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and execute awards,
purchase orders or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. These funds
shall remain available for this purpose for eighteen months from the date of this
Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency
Fund.
D. The Lieutenant Governor's verbal orders activating the National Guard and authorizing
the utilization of National Guard assets to fight the East Peak Fire and enforce the laws
of the State of Colorado as provided in C.R.S. § 28-3-104 are hereby memorialized by
this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were
contained within this Executive Order.
E. The Colorado Department of Public Safety is authorized and directed to coordinate
application to the federal government for funds available for reimbursement and to
coordinate application for any other funds available related to this disaster emergency.
F. My verbal order approving the movement of the Spanish Peaks Regional Medical
Center, including pharmaceuticals, to an alternate facility is hereby memorialized by this
Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained
within this Executive Order. The provisions of Title 12, Article 42.5, Part 1, and the
corresponding Board of Pharmacy Rules and regulations pertaining to the authorized
persons, outlets and orders for the compounding, dispensing and delivery of any drug
are hereby suspended for the purpose of rapidly distributing medications to actual or
potential victims of the current fire emergency and evacuated area in Huerfano and Las
Animas Counties. A hospital outlet is authorized to transfer its prescription drug
inventory to a distribution site outside the hospital as required by the Executive Director
or Chief Medical Officer of the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment
(CDPHE) or the director of a local health department.
G. I am suspending state requirements regarding licensed health facility bed capacities and
configuration for facilities accepting patients from evacuated facilities. Such facilities
shall notify the CDPHE of bed number changes at their earliest convenience within 72
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2013-013
June 21, 2013
Page 4 of 4
hours. I am also suspending Colorado EMS provider certification for personnel directly
in support of wildfire suppression operations in the State of Colorado who hold current
EMS provider certification from any state or territory in the United States until this
executive order expires, unless extended as provided in Section III.
III.
Duration

available for the described purposes for eighteen months from the date of this Executive Order.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-
33.5-701, et seq., and specifically C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704, I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the
State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending the availability of funds to pay
costs associated with the disaster emergencies due to wildfires that occurred in Colorado
during 2011 and 2012.
Background and Purpose
In 2011 and 2012, Colorado experienced extraordinary wildfire seasons due to dry
conditions and high temperatures. In this time period, over twenty-five wildfires required a
declaration of a disaster emergency. These wildfires resulted in a record breaking number of
fatalities and damage to homes, forest land, and agricultural assets. On July 1, 2012, the
Colorado State Forest Service fire-management functions for command and control were
transferred from Colorado State University to the Colorado Department of Public Safety.
Currently, there is a vacancy in the position assigned to review federal invoices for fires.
Due to the aforementioned circumstances, the final payments for 2011 and 2012 fires will not
be completed prior to the expiration dates in the associated Executive Orders. This Executive
Order extends the expiration dates of the previously approved funding for these wildfires.
Specifically this Executive Order extends the funding for the following wildfires and their
associated Executive Orders:
• Purgatoire - D 2011-015
• Bear - D 2011-015
• Navajo - D 2011-021
• Brice - D 2011-022
• Shell Fire Complex - D 2011-022
• Mesa de Maya - D 2011-022
• Duckett - D 2011-023

• Lower North Fork - D 2012-007 and D 2012-008
• Hewlett - D 2012-011 and D 2012-012
• Stuart Hole - D 2012-017
• Springer - D 2012-018
• Weber - D 2012-021
• Flagstaff - D 2012-023 and D2012-038
• Pine Ridge - D 2012-025
• Bull Basin - D 2012-032
• Powell Complex - D 2012-034
• Wetmore - D 2012-044 and D 2012-045
• Roatcap - D 2012-046
Declaration and Directives
In addition to the declarations and directives contained in the Executive Orders cited
above, I declare and direct, as follows:
A.
I extend the funding in the Disaster Emergency Fund provided in the cited
Executive Orders until January 31, 2014, to facilitate final payments of the
expenses associated with these wildfires. The Division of Fire Prevention and
Control and the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management are
authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate resources as
may be appropriate and permitted by law.
B.
Any unexpended funds remaining after final payments or on February 1, 2014,
whichever occurs first, will be allocated as provided in the original Executive
Orders previously cited.
III.
Duration
The funds made available in the original Executive Orders cited shall remain available
until January 31, 2014, and in all other respects the cited Executive Orders shall remain in full
force and effect as originally promulgated.

Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in
particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104 and relevant portions of the
Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., 1, Joseph A. Garcia, Lieutenant
Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of
disaster emergency due to the West Fork Fire Complex in Mineral, Rio Grande, and Hinsdale
Counties, Colorado and making resources available to fight the fire and address the disaster
emergency.
Background and Purpose
The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented
by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or
imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting
from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to ... fire."
C.R.S. §24-33.5-703(3).
On June 5, 2013, lightning started the West Fork Fire on the San Juan National Forest in Mineral
County. By June 14, 2013, the West Fork Fire grew to approximately 30 acres and the Windy
Pass Fire also ignited and grew to approximately 3 acres across Highway 160 from the West
Fork Fire near Windy Pass. By June 16, 2013, the West Fork Fire grew to approximately 1,747
acres and the Windy Pass Fire grew to 108 acres. The San Juan National Forest combined the
fires to form the West Fork Fire Complex and ordered a National Incident Management
Organization Team to manage the fire.
On June 20, 2013, extreme fire weather conditions caused the West Fork Fire Complex to grow
to over 29,000 acres and cross over the Continental Divide into the Rio Grande National Forest
---PAGE---
Executive Order D 2013-017
June 26, 2013
Page 2 of 5
and Rio Grande County. This resulted in a mandatory evacuation east of the Continental Divide
to the town limits of South Fork, Colorado and the voluntary evacuation of the town of South
Park. Because of continuing fire growth, the Town of South Park received a mandatory
evacuation order at 0600 hours on June 21, 2013. All available firefighting resources were
committed to firefighting and structural protection.
On June 20, 2013, at approximately 2000 hours, the Mineral and Rio Grande Counties Sheriffs
determined that the fire had extended from the San Juan and Rio Grande National Forests and
would exceed the ability of the counties and other local resources to contain and extinguish it
and requested the response of the Division of Fire Prevention and Control. The Mineral and Rio
Grande Counties Sheriffs requested transfer of the fire to the State of Colorado under the
Emergency Fire Fund (EFF) provisions.
